work: Enarratio in Epistolam II B. Pauli ad Corinthios
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: Expositio primi capituli: Paulus apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei
1.title_en: Explanation of the first chapter: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God

paras.t: Quoniam Corinthiorum nonnulli minus digne de Paulo senserunt, atque ob hoc propriam salutem neglexerunt, parvi pendentes verba Pauli, et pseudoapostolis credentes ; idcirco in exordio hujus epistolæ, in qua more solito præmittitur salutatio, quum dixisset, Paulus, statim adjecit, Apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei, non ut se ipsum magnificaret, sed ut illorum provideret saluti. Potest enim, et dum ratio postulat, debet prælatus auctoritatem suam ostendere, ne sui contemptus impediat subditorum salutem.
paras.en: Since some of the Corinthians thought less worthily of Paul than they ought, and on that account neglected their own salvation, setting little store by Paul's words and believing the false apostles, therefore at the opening of this epistle, in which the greeting is set first as usual, when he had said [[1:1|Paul|Paulus]], he at once added [[1:1|an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God|Apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei]]: not to magnify himself, but to provide for their salvation. For a prelate may, and when reason demands it must, show his authority, lest contempt of him hinder the salvation of those under him.

paras.t: Ponens ergo Apostolus personas scribentes seu salutantes, ait : Paulus apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei, id est a Deo seu divina voluntate ad gratiam apostolatus assumptus, non a se ipso vel ab hominibus intrusus inordinate. Timotheus Ephesiorum episcopus, frater noster spiritualis. Hunc sibi adjungit Apostolus, ne Corinthii aliquid sinistrum suspicentur de eo, quasi eos accusaverit apud Apostolum ex rancore. Priorem enim epistolam tulit Corinthiis, redeuntesque nuntiavit Apostolo facta et verba Corinthiorum. Quamvis autem Apostolus solus istam epistolam dictaverit, uterque tamen mandat et mittit eam Corinthiis : et forte quia Paulus multa scribit ex Timothei relatu. Itaque, Paulus et Timotheus mandant Ecclesiæ Dei, id est congregationi fidelium, quæ est Corinthi, id est in civitate sic dicta, metropolitana Achaiæ, cum sanctis omnibus, id est et sanctis omnibus, utpote cunctis veraciter christianis, qui utique sancti et virtuosi sunt, qui sunt, id est demorantur, in universa Achaia, id est quocumque loco provinciæ sic vocatæ, quæ erat pars Græciæ.
paras.en: Setting down, then, the persons who write or greet, the Apostle says: [[1:1|Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God|Paulus apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei]], that is, taken up to the grace of the apostleship by God, or by the divine will, not thrust in disorderly by himself or by men. [[1:1|and Timothy|Timotheus]], bishop of the Ephesians, [[1:1|our brother|frater]] in the spirit. The Apostle joins him to himself lest the Corinthians suspect something ill of him, as though he had accused them to the Apostle out of rancour. For he had carried the earlier epistle to the Corinthians, and on his return reported to the Apostle the deeds and words of the Corinthians. And although the Apostle alone dictated this epistle, both of them nevertheless commit it and send it to the Corinthians: and perhaps because Paul writes many things from Timothy's report. So Paul and Timothy send [[1:1|to the church of God|Ecclesiæ Dei]], that is, to the congregation of the faithful, [[1:1|that is at Corinth|quæ est Corinthi]], that is, in the city so called, the metropolis of Achaia, [[1:1|with all the saints|cum sanctis omnibus]], that is, and to all the saints, namely to all who are truly Christians, who indeed are holy and virtuous, [[1:1|that are|qui sunt]], that is, who dwell, [[1:1|in all Achaia|in universa Achaia]], that is, in whatever place of the province so called, which was a part of Greece.

paras.t: Gratia, quæ est supernaturalis habitus, principium omnis meritoriæ operationis, essentiam animæ immediate perficiens, vobis præstetur : et pax, id est tranquillitas mentis : de qua angeli cecinerunt : Et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis ; a Deo Patre nostro per gratiam adoptionis, id est a tota superbenedicta Trinitate, quæ est unus verus Deus, creator et pater noster, cui quotidie dicimus : Pater noster, qui es in cœlis : et Domino nostro Jesu Christo, id est per Christum mediatorem Dei ac hominum, per quem omnis gloria nobis confertur. Christus enim ut Deus, est idem collator principalis cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto ; sed secundum naturam assumptam, est dator gratiæ mediatus ac instrumentalis, quia per ipsum tanquam per causam meritoriam ac mediatricem, dantur nobis charismata Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: [[1:2|Grace|Gratia]], which is a supernatural habit, the principle of every meritorious work, perfecting the essence of the soul immediately [that is, grace inheres in the very substance of the soul, not first in one of its powers], be granted [[1:2|unto you|vobis]]: [[1:2|and peace|et pax]], that is, tranquillity of mind: of which the angels sang: And [[Luke 2:14|on earth peace to men of good will|in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis]]; [[1:2|from God our Father|a Deo Patre nostro]] by the grace of adoption, that is, from the whole superblessed Trinity, which is the one true God, our Creator and Father, to whom we say daily: [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven|Pater noster, qui es in cœlis]]; [[1:2|and from the Lord Jesus Christ|et Domino nostro Jesu Christo]], that is, through Christ the mediator of God and men, through whom all glory is conferred on us. For Christ as God is the same principal giver together with the Father and the Holy Ghost; but according to the nature he assumed, he is the mediate and instrumental giver of grace, because through him, as through the meritorious and mediating cause, the gifts of the Holy Ghost are given us.

paras.t: Consequenter procedit Apostolus ad narrationem, captatque benevolentiam Corinthiorum, et a gratiarum actione incipiens, affatur perfectos. Benedictus Deus, id est, ab omnibus benedicatur et exaltetur, semperque sit benedictus Deus Trinitas, et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est persona Patris æterni, qui est genitor Christi secundum ejus divinam naturam. Hunc Patrem Apostolus specialiter exprimit exemplo Christi, qui per totum Evangelium omnia refert specialiter ad gloriam Patris, quemadmodum ait : Honorifico Patrem meum. Non quod Pater major sit Filio aut Spiritui Sancto, sed quia auctoritas est in Patre, atque fontalis origo, respectu Filii et Spiritus Sancti, quorum uterque suscepit a Patre quidquid habet et est. Vel sic : Benedictus Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est persona Patris, qui est Deus Christi secundum naturam humanam, et Pater ipsius secundum naturam divinam. Unde in Evangelio Christus testatur : Ascendo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum, Deum meum et Deum vestrum. Vel, Deus, ratione essentiæ et emanationis ad extra : Pater vero, ratione proprietatis relativæ et emanationis ad intra. Porro quod subditur, simili sensu accipi potest, tam de persona Patris, quam de tota Trinitate, Patre nostro ratione creationis, gubernationis et adoptationis.
paras.en: Next the Apostle proceeds to the narration [that is, the body of the letter, after the greeting], wins the goodwill of the Corinthians, and, beginning with thanksgiving, addresses the perfect. [[1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], that is, may God the Trinity be blessed and exalted by all, and be blessed for ever, [[1:3|and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ|et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, the person of the eternal Father, who is the begetter of Christ according to his divine nature. The Apostle names this Father in particular after the example of Christ, who throughout the Gospel refers all things in particular to the glory of the Father, as he says: [[John 8:49|I honour my Father|Honorifico Patrem meum]]. Not that the Father is greater than the Son or the Holy Ghost, but because authority is in the Father, and he is the fountain-source with respect to the Son and the Holy Ghost, each of whom received from the Father whatever he has and is. Or thus: [[1:3|Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ|Benedictus Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, the person of the Father, who is the God of Christ according to his human nature, and his Father according to his divine nature. Hence Christ testifies in the Gospel: [[John 20:17|I ascend to my Father and to your Father, to my God and to your God|Ascendo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum, Deum meum et Deum vestrum]]. Or: God, by reason of the essence and of the outward procession [that is, his working in creatures]; but Father, by reason of the relative property and of the inward procession [that is, the begetting of the Son within the Godhead]. Further, what follows can be taken in a like sense, both of the person of the Father and of the whole Trinity, our Father by reason of creation, governance and adoption.

paras.t: Pater misericordiarum, id est causa paterna piorum affectuum ex divina benignitate manantium ; vel, Pater misericordiarum intransitive, id est Pater multum misericors seu misericordia plenus. Et dicitur, Pater misericordiarum, quamvis misericordia Dei sit una ac simplex, propter diversos effectus pietatis divinæ. Unde etiam ait Psalmista : Misericordias Domini in æternum cantabo. Et Deus totius consolationis, id est dator atque benignus infusor omnis veræ, perfectæ ac spiritualis consolationis sive lætitiæ, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra, quam propter justitiam patimur a mundo, carne aut diabolo. Consolatur autem nos, vel a tribulationibus liberando, vel in tribulationibus patientiam dando, ita ut omne gaudium æstimemus quum diversas inciderimus tentationes ; vel in ipso corde copiosam exsultationem concitando ex contemplatione divinorum, sic ut tribulationis acerbitas vix sentiatur. Hinc scriptum est in Job : Ipse vulnerat, et medetur ; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt. Et Habacuc propheta orat : Quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis.
paras.en: [[1:3|The Father of mercies|Pater misericordiarum]], that is, the fatherly cause of the loving affections that flow from the divine kindness; or, Father of mercies taken intransitively [that is, as saying what he is rather than what he causes], that is, a Father very merciful, or full of mercy. And he is called Father of mercies, though the mercy of God is one and simple, because of the diverse effects of the divine pity. Hence also the Psalmist says: [[Ps 88:2|The mercies of the Lord I will sing for ever|Misericordias Domini in æternum cantabo]]. [[1:3|and the God of all comfort|Et Deus totius consolationis]], that is, the giver and kindly pourer-in of all true, perfect and spiritual consolation or joy, [[1:4|Who comforteth us in all our tribulation|qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra]], which we suffer for justice' sake from the world, the flesh or the devil. Now he comforts us either by freeing us from tribulations, or by giving patience in tribulations, so that we count it all joy when we fall into divers temptations[[Jas 1:2||]]; or by stirring up abundant exultation in the heart itself from the contemplation of divine things, so that the bitterness of tribulation is scarcely felt. Hence it is written in Job: [[Job 5:18|he woundeth, and cureth: he striketh, and his hands shall heal|Ipse vulnerat, et medetur ; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt]]. And Habacuc the prophet prays: [[Hab 3:2|when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy|Quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis]].

paras.t: Ut possimus et ipsi consolari eos : id est, tam copiose et ad hoc consolatur Deus nos Apostolos, virosque perfectos, ut ex plenitudine, gustu et experientia consolationis nobis infusæ, valeamus et nos consolari eos qui in omni pressura sunt, in quacumque afflictione, proponendo nos eis in exemplum : possimus, inquam, consolari eos per exhortationem qua exhortamur et ipsi a Deo, id est admonendo eos taliter per prædicationem vocalem, sicut admonemur a Domino per inspirationem seu allocutionem internam : videlicet, commemorando præmia sempiterna pro præsentibus brevibusque tribulationibus rependenda, proponendo etiam persecutiones passionesque Christi et aliorum electorum pro exemplo, quemadmodum retulit Judith : Memores (inquiens) esse debent, quomodo pater noster Abraham tentatus est, et omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles.
paras.en: [[1:4|that we also may be able to comfort them|Ut possimus et ipsi consolari eos]]: that is, God comforts us apostles and perfect men so abundantly, and to this end, that from the fulness, the taste and the experience of the consolation poured into us we too may be able to comfort them [[1:4|who are in all distress|qui in omni pressura sunt]], in whatever affliction, by setting ourselves before them as an example: we may be able, I say, to comfort them [[1:4|by the exhortation wherewith we also are exhorted by God|per exhortationem qua exhortamur et ipsi a Deo]], that is, by admonishing them through spoken preaching in the same way as we are admonished by the Lord through inspiration or inward speech: namely, by recalling the everlasting rewards to be paid back for present and brief tribulations, and also by setting forth as an example the persecutions and sufferings of Christ and of the other elect, as Judith related: [[Jdt 8:22|They must remember|Memores]] (she says) [[Jdt 8:22|how our father Abraham was tempted|esse debent, quomodo pater noster Abraham tentatus est]], [[Jdt 8:23|and all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|et omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]].

paras.t: Elucescit autem ex his, quia alios spiritualiter consolari aptus non est, qui divinam consolationem expertus non est. Ideo per Sapientem dicitur : Vir in multis expertus cogitabit multa. Verumtamen aliqui ad Deum conversi, tribulantur, tentantur et angustiantur ; nullam tamen consolationem experiuntur : quibus cælum est æneum, terraque ferrea ; qui cum beato Job Domino dicere possunt : Sto, et non respicis me ; clamo, et non exaudis me : mutatus es mihi in crudelem. Sed isti non desperent, non frangantur, nec pusillanimes fiant, sed manum Domini longanimiter præstolentur, scientes quod Deus non deserat sperantes in se, dicentesque cum Job : Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo. Interim vero carnalem consolationem despiciant, quatenus in Dei contemplatione refloreant, juxta illud in Psalmo : Renuit consolari anima mea ; memor fui Dei, et delectatus sum.
paras.en: It is clear from this that he is not fit to console others spiritually who has not himself experienced the divine consolation. Therefore it is said by the Wise Man: [[Ecclus 34:9|A man that hath much experience, shall think of many things|Vir in multis expertus cogitabit multa]]. Yet some who have turned to God are afflicted, tempted and straitened, and still experience no consolation: for them the heaven is brass and the earth iron; they can say to the Lord with blessed Job: [[Job 30:20|I stand up, and thou dost not regard me|Sto, et non respicis me]]; I cry, [[Job 30:20|and thou hearest me not|et non exaudis me]]: [[Job 30:21|Thou art changed to be cruel toward me|mutatus es mihi in crudelem]]. But let these not despair, nor be broken, nor grow faint-hearted, but wait with long patience for the hand of the Lord, knowing that God does not forsake them that hope in him[[Jdt 13:17||]], and saying with Job: [[Job 13:15|Although he should kill me, I will trust in him|Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo]]. Meanwhile let them despise fleshly consolation, so that they may flower again in the contemplation of God, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 76:3|My soul refused to be comforted|Renuit consolari anima mea]]; [[Ps 76:4|I remembered God, and was delighted|memor fui Dei, et delectatus sum]].

paras.t: Denique, quod consolemur a Deo, aliosque consolari possimus, patet ex hoc : Quoniam sicut abundant passiones Christi, id est persecutiones quæ in Christo capite nostro præcesserunt, et propter eum fidelibus infliguntur, ejus quoque amore æquanimiter tolerantur, in nobis famulis Christi, quibus ipse ait : Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur, quia non est servus major domino suo ; ita et per Christum, id est per gratiam et misericordiam Christi, abundat consolatio nostra. Qui enim compatitur, et conglorificabitur. Propterea dicit Propheta : Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam. Alibi quoque dicit Scriptura : Qui derelictus est in ira Dei omnipotentis, iterum in magna reconciliatione cum summa gloria exaltabitur.
paras.en: Lastly, that we are comforted by God and can comfort others is clear from this: [[1:5|For as the sufferings of Christ abound|Quoniam sicut abundant passiones Christi]], that is, the persecutions which went before in Christ our head, and are inflicted on the faithful for his sake, and are also borne with an even mind for love of him, [[1:5|in us|in nobis]], the servants of Christ, to whom he himself says: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]], for [[John 15:20|The servant is not greater than his master|non est servus major domino suo]][[John 16:33||]]; [[1:5|so also by Christ|ita et per Christum]], that is, by the grace and mercy of Christ, [[1:5|doth our comfort abound|abundat consolatio nostra]]. For he who suffers with him will also be glorified with him[[Rom 8:17||]]. Therefore the Prophet says: [[Ps 93:19|According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, thy comforts have given joy to my soul.|Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam.]]. Elsewhere too the Scripture says: He that [[2 Mach 5:20|was forsaken in the wrath of Almighty God|derelictus est in ira Dei omnipotentis]], [[2 Mach 5:20|shall be exalted again with great glory, when the great Lord shall be reconciled|iterum in magna reconciliatione cum summa gloria exaltabitur]] [Denis reads: shall be exalted again with the highest glory in a great reconciliation].

paras.t: Sive autem tribulamur, tribulatio ista accidit nobis pro vestra exhortatione et salute, id est, utilis est ad exhortandum vos salubriter, scilicet ut vos exemplo nostri tribulationes sustineatis libenter ; sive consolamur a Deo, hoc fit pro vestra consolatione, id est, utile est ad consolandum vos, quoniam eadem merces nobis et vobis promittitur ; sive exhortamur, id est, divinitus admonemur omnia […] perpeti, hoc fit pro vestra exhortatione et salute, quia per hoc idonei efficimur admonere vos ad vestram salutem, sicut et ipsi a Deo monemur ; quæ exhortatio operatur in vobis tolerantiam earumdem passionum, id est, inducit et provocat vos ad tolerandum pro Christo persecutiones et adversitates, quas et nos patimur :
paras.en: [[1:6|Now whether we be in tribulation|Sive autem tribulamur]], this tribulation befalls us [[1:6|for your exhortation and salvation|pro vestra exhortatione et salute]], that is, it serves to exhort you to your salvation, namely that by our example you may bear tribulations willingly; [[1:6|or whether we be comforted|sive consolamur]] by God, this is done [[1:6|for your consolation|pro vestra consolatione]], that is, it serves to console you, since the same reward is promised to us and to you; [[1:6|or whether we be exhorted|sive exhortamur]], that is, are admonished by God to suffer all things […], this is done [[1:6|for your exhortation and salvation|pro vestra exhortatione et salute]], because by this we are made fit to admonish you for your salvation, as we ourselves are admonished by God; [[1:6|which worketh|quæ exhortatio operatur]] in you [[1:6|the enduring of the same sufferings|tolerantiam earumdem passionum]], that is, which leads and stirs you to endure persecutions and adversities for Christ, [[1:6|which we also suffer|quas et nos patimur]]:

paras.t: ut et spes nostra, id est fiducia qua speramus vos beatitudinem adepturos, firma, id est constans et efficax, sit pro vobis, id est ad commodum vestrum. Dum enim prælati conspiciunt subditos suos in virtutibus agiles, secure et firmiter sperant bona æterna eis fore parata. Unde et Salomon : Filius sapiens lætificat patrem. Scientes, certitudine revelationis divinæ et experientiæ, non ratiocinationis humanæ (de qua scientia ait Job : Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum), quoniam, id est quod, sicut socii, id est participes et consortes, estis passionum, id est tribulationum pro Christo, imitando ejus vestigia, sic eritis et socii consolationis divinæ per gratiam Christi in præsenti inchoative et imperfecte, in futuro autem plene ac jugiter. Si enim sustinemus, et conregnabimus. Ideo scriptum est : Communicantes Christi passionibus gaudete, ut et in revelatione gloriæ ejus gaudeatis.
paras.en: [[1:7|That our hope|ut et spes nostra]], that is, the confidence with which we hope that you will attain beatitude, [[1:7|may be steadfast|firma]], that is, constant and effective, [[1:7|for you|sit pro vobis]], that is, to your advantage. For when prelates see those under them quick in the virtues, they hope securely and firmly that eternal goods are prepared for them. Hence Solomon too: [[Prov 10:1|A wise son maketh the father glad|Filius sapiens lætificat patrem]]. [[1:7|knowing|Scientes]], with the certainty of divine revelation and of experience, not of human reasoning (of which knowledge Job says: [[Job 19:25|I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]]), [[1:7|that|quoniam]] [Denis glosses the lemma's quoniam with the plainer quod; both mean "that"], [[1:7|as you are partakers|sicut socii]], that is, sharers and companions, [[1:7|of the sufferings|estis passionum]], that is, of tribulations for Christ, by following in his footsteps, [[1:7|so shall you be also of the consolation|sic eritis et socii consolationis]] of God, through the grace of Christ: in the present in a beginning and imperfect way, but in the future fully and unceasingly. For [[2 Tim 2:12|if we suffer, we shall also reign|sustinemus, et conregnabimus]]. Therefore it is written: If you [[1 Pet 4:13|partake of the sufferings of Christ, rejoice that, when his glory shall be revealed, you may also be glad|Communicantes Christi passionibus gaudete, ut et in revelatione gloriæ ejus gaudeatis]].

paras.t: Præterea narrat Apostolus magnitudinem persecutionum suarum in speciali : primo, ut alii exemplo sui ad patientiam animentur : secundo, ut discipulis insinuet quanta pro eorum patiatur salute ; tertio, ut nos, advertentes quam modicum patiamur comparatione Apostoli, ab inordinato mœrore cessemus. Itaque ait : Nolo […] enim vos ignorare, fratres […]. Apostolus discipulos suos nominat filios, sæpe autem fratres. In quo perstringitur quorumdam superiorum superbia, qui nimium proni sunt vocare subditos suos, filios, non tam ex paterna dilectione, quam ex quadam animositate […] ad Scripturam recurrentes dicunt : Nolite extolli ; esto in illis quasi unus ex ipsis. Nolo ergo vos ignorare de tribulatione nostra quæ facta est, id est, nobis illata est, in Asia, id est in Epheso urbe Asiæ, ab Alexandro argentario qui fecit ædes Dianæ : de qua tribulatione multa scripta sunt in Actibus ; quoniam supra modum solitum gravati sumus, et supra virtutem naturalem atque humanam : non tamen ultra virtutem nobis per gratiam communicatam, quia supra dictum est : Fidelis Deus, qui non patietur vos tentari supra id quod potestis ; ita ut tæderet nos etiam vivere, secundum inferiorem partem animæ, scilicet sensualitatem, vel sensitivum appetitum (quemadmodum scriptum est de Christo : Cœpit Jesus pavere et tædere) : non tamen secundum rationem fide et spe adornatam, quia hoc esset contra patientiæ perfectionem.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle relates the greatness of his persecutions in particular: first, that others may be roused to patience by his example; secondly, to make known to his disciples how much he suffers for their salvation; thirdly, that we, noticing how little we suffer in comparison with the Apostle, may cease from inordinate grief. And so he says: [[1:8|For we would not have you ignorant|Nolo […] enim vos ignorare]] […], [[1:8|brethren|fratres]] […]. The Apostle names his disciples sons, but often brethren [the sense seems to want "seldom" or "sometimes" before "names": the word may be among those lost just before]. In this is rebuked the pride of certain superiors, who are all too ready to call those under them sons, not so much out of fatherly love as out of a certain arrogance […], having recourse to the Scripture, say: [[Ecclus 32:1|be not lifted up|Nolite extolli]]; [[Ecclus 32:1|be among them as one of them|esto in illis quasi unus ex ipsis]]. I would not, then, have you ignorant [[1:8|of our tribulation which came to us|de tribulatione nostra quæ facta est]], that is, which was inflicted on us, [[1:8|in Asia|in Asia]], that is, at Ephesus, a city of Asia, by Alexander the silversmith who made the temples of Diana[[Acts 19:24||]] [in the Acts the silversmith is Demetrius; an Alexander is put forward in the same riot, Acts 19:33]: of which tribulation much is written in the Acts; [[1:8|that we were pressed out of measure|quoniam supra modum solitum gravati sumus]], beyond the usual, [[1:8|above our strength|et supra virtutem]], natural and human: yet not beyond the strength given us by grace, for it was said above [that is, in the first epistle to the Corinthians]: [[1 Cor 10:13|God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able|Fidelis Deus, qui non patietur vos tentari supra id quod potestis]]; [[1:8|so that we were weary even of life|ita ut tæderet nos etiam vivere]], according to the lower part of the soul, namely the sensuality or sensitive appetite (as it is written of Christ: Jesus [[Mark 14:33|began to fear and to be heavy|Cœpit Jesus pavere et tædere]]): yet not according to the reason, adorned with faith and hope, for that would be against the perfection of patience.

paras.t: Posset præterea scisciari quis hoc loco, an liceat homini mortem optare propter adversitatum acerbitatem. Et primo apparet quod sic, auctoritate Apostoli loco præsenti. Secundo, quoniam Elias persecutionem Jezabel fugiens, dixit : Sufficit mihi, Domine, tolle animam meam. Tobias quoque excæcatus, oravit : Præcipe, Domine, in pace recipi spiritum meum. Simili modo Job ait : Elegit suspendium anima mea, et mortem ossa mea. Et respondendum, quod non licet propter persecutiones vitandas optare mortem absolute, et sicut terminum vitæ. Licet tamen sub conditione, videlicet divina voluntate supposita, et mortem considerando tanquam ingressum vitæ futuræ : sic tamen, ut quamvis persecutio sit occasio hujus desiderii, caritas sit præcipiens atque eliciens actum hunc.
paras.en: Further, someone might ask at this place whether it is lawful for a man to wish for death because of the bitterness of adversities. And first it appears that it is, by the authority of the Apostle in the present place. Secondly, because Elias, fleeing the persecution of Jezabel, said: [[3 Kings 19:4|It is enough for me, Lord; take away my soul|Sufficit mihi, Domine, tolle animam meam]]. Tobias also, when he was blinded, prayed: [[Tob 3:6|Command|Præcipe]], O Lord, [[Tob 3:6|my spirit to be received in peace|in pace recipi spiritum meum]]. In like manner Job says: [[Job 7:15|my soul rather chooseth hanging, and my bones death|Elegit suspendium anima mea, et mortem ossa mea]]. And the answer is that it is not lawful to wish for death absolutely, and as the end of life, in order to escape persecutions. It is lawful, however, under a condition, namely supposing the divine will, and considering death as the entrance into the life to come: yet so that, though persecution be the occasion of this desire, charity is what commands and elicits this act [that is, the wish to die must spring from the love of God, not from flight from suffering].

paras.t: Sed et ipsi, id est ego et adhærentes mihi, in nobis responsum mortis habuimus, id est, ex persecutionis illius consideratione animus noster nobis respondit, et certe putavimus, quod mors nobis instaret : non enim arbitrabamur nos posse evadere. Quod ideo Deus permisit, ut non simus fidentes in nobis, id est, ne in propria potestate speremus : Maledictus enim, inquit Jeremias, qui confidit in homine ; sed in Deo. Unde per Isaiam quoque dicitur : Quis ambulat in tenebris, et non est ei lumen? speret in nomine Domini, et innitatur super Deum suum. Et Jeremias iterum : Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino. Qui suscitat mortuos corporaliter, animam iterum corpori uniendo, et spiritualiter, caritatem et gratiam peccatoribus conferendo. De talibus spiritualiter mortuis Christus in Evangelio loquitur : Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos.
paras.en: [[1:9|But we|Sed et ipsi]], that is, I and those who hold to me, [[1:9|had in ourselves the answer of death|in nobis responsum mortis habuimus]], that is, from considering that persecution our mind answered us, and we surely thought that death was upon us: for we did not think we could escape. God allowed this [[1:9|that we should not trust in ourselves|ut non simus fidentes in nobis]], that is, lest we hope in our own power: for [[Jer 17:5|Cursed|Maledictus]], says Jeremias, is he [[Jer 17:5|that trusteth in man|qui confidit in homine]]; [[1:9|but in God|sed in Deo]]. Hence it is said by Isaias also: Who [[Is 50:10|hath walked in darkness, and hath no light?|ambulat in tenebris, et non est ei lumen?]]? [[Is 50:10|let him hope in the name of the Lord, and lean upon his God|speret in nomine Domini, et innitatur super Deum suum]]. And Jeremias again: [[Jer 17:7|Blessed be the man that trusteth in the Lord|Benedictus vir qui confidit in Domino]]. [[1:9|who raiseth the dead|Qui suscitat mortuos]], bodily, by uniting the soul to the body again, and spiritually, by bestowing charity and grace on sinners. Of such as are spiritually dead Christ speaks in the Gospel: [[Matt 8:22|let the dead bury their dead|Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos]].

paras.t: Qui de tantis periculis vitæ corporalis eripuit nos in Epheso, et eruit incessanter, quum tribulamur. In quem speramus, id est, de cujus bonitate confidimus, quoniam et adhuc eripiet in futuro a similibus periculis. Non quod Apostolus a tribulationibus erui concupivit, quasi mortem pro Christo pati imparatus, sed quia in carne manere necessarium fuit propter discipulos.
paras.en: [[1:10|Who|Qui]] [[1:10|out of so great dangers|de tantis periculis]] of bodily life [[1:10|hath delivered|eripuit nos]] us at Ephesus, [[1:10|and doth deliver|et eruit]] us unceasingly, when we are afflicted. [[1:10|in whom we trust|In quem speramus]], that is, in whose goodness we confide, [[1:10|that he will yet also deliver us|quoniam et adhuc eripiet]] in time to come from like dangers. Not that the Apostle longed to be delivered from tribulations, as though he were unready to suffer death for Christ, but because it was needful to abide in the flesh for his disciples' sake[[Phil 1:24||]].

paras.t: Eripiet ergo nos, adjuvantibus et vobis in oratione fusa pro nobis, id est vestra oratione nobis succurrente, et istam ereptionem nobis promerente seu impetrante ad hunc finem, ut ex multarum personis facierum, id est a personis diversarum dispositionum, ætatum, virtutum, meritorum atque respectuum, scilicet a cunctis gradibus fidelium, qui sunt ejus quæ in nobis est donationis, id est gratiæ nobis divinitus distributæ, participes, per multos, id est ab his diversis pluribusque fidelibus, gratiæ agantur Deo pro nobis, id est pro nostri ereptione : videlicet, ut omnes fideles gratias referant Deo pro conservatione vitæ meæ ad profectum eorum. Et merito hoc agere debent, dignumque est sic fieri :
paras.en: He will deliver us, then, [[1:11|You helping withal in prayer for us|adjuvantibus et vobis in oratione fusa pro nobis]] [Denis reads "in prayer poured out for us"], that is, your prayer coming to our aid, and meriting or obtaining this deliverance for us, to this end: [[1:11|That|ut]] [[1:11|by the means of many persons|ex multarum personis facierum]] [Denis's text reads "from the persons of many faces"], that is, from persons of diverse dispositions, ages, virtues, merits and standing, namely from all ranks of the faithful, who are partakers of that [[1:11|gift|ejus quæ in nobis est donationis]] which is in us, that is, of the grace bestowed on us by God, [[1:11|by many|per multos]], that is, by these diverse and numerous faithful, [[1:11|thanks may be given|gratiæ agantur]] to God [[1:11|in our behalf|pro nobis]], that is, for our deliverance: namely, that all the faithful may give thanks to God for the preserving of my life for their progress. And rightly ought they to do this, and it is fitting that it be so:

paras.t: Nam gloria nostra, id est causa atque materia nostræ spiritualis exsultationis in Deo, hæc est, testimonium conscientiæ nostræ, id est fiducialis testificatio conscientiæ propriæ. Secura enim mens, quasi juge convivium. Semper vero præsumit sæva conscientia perturbata. Deinde ponit quid sibi perhibeat atque testetur conscientia sua, videlicet : quod in simplicitate bona, quæ duplicitatis plicam excludit, et sinceritate, id est munda intentione ac pura veritate, Dei, et non in sapientia carnali aut sæculari, quæ docet sensibilia bona exquirere : de qua dicitur, Non est ista sapientia desursum, sed terrena, animalis et diabolica ; sed in gratia Dei, id est secundum instinctum et opera gratiæ nobis a Deo infusæ, conversati sumus in hoc mundo, a tempore conversionis nostræ ad Christum, abundantius autem, id est, gratiosius conversati sumus, ad vos, id est vobiscum, a quibus nihil recepimus. De hac laudabili simplicitate, qua homo corde, ore et opere, uniformi modo se habet, omnem vitans simulationem hypocritarum, scriptum est in Proverbiis : Recti habitabunt in terra, et simplices permanebunt in ea ; et iterum : Cum simplicibus sermocinatio Dei. Ad hanc simplicitatem hortatur Jacobus, dicens : Purificate corda, duplices animo. Porro, quod ita habuerimus nos ad vos, patet :
paras.en: [[1:12|For our glory|Nam gloria nostra]], that is, the cause and matter of our spiritual exultation in God, [[1:12|is this: the testimony of our conscience|hæc est, testimonium conscientiæ nostræ]], that is, the confident witness of one's own conscience. For [[Prov 15:15|a secure mind is like a continual feast|Secura enim mens, quasi juge convivium]]. But [[Wis 17:10|a troubled conscience always forecasteth grievous things|Semper vero præsumit sæva conscientia perturbata]]. Then he sets down what his conscience bears witness to and testifies for him, namely: [[1:12|that in simplicity|quod in simplicitate bona]] [Denis reads "in good simplicity", where the Vulgate has "simplicity of heart"], which shuts out the fold of doubleness [a play on duplicitas, "doubleness", and plica, "fold"], [[1:12|and sincerity|et sinceritate]], that is, with clean intention and pure truth, [[1:12|of God, and not in carnal wisdom|Dei, et non in sapientia carnali]] or worldly wisdom, which teaches men to seek out the goods of sense: of which it is said: [[Jas 3:15|this is not wisdom|Non est ista sapientia]] from above, [[Jas 3:15|but earthly, sensual, devilish|sed terrena, animalis et diabolica]]; [[1:12|but in the grace of God|sed in gratia Dei]], that is, according to the prompting and the works of the grace poured into us by God, [[1:12|we have conversed in this world|conversati sumus in hoc mundo]], from the time of our conversion to Christ, [[1:12|and more abundantly|abundantius autem]], that is, we have conducted ourselves more graciously, [[1:12|towards you|ad vos]], that is, among you, from whom we have received nothing. Of this praiseworthy simplicity, by which a man is the same in heart, mouth and deed, shunning all the pretence of hypocrites, it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 2:21|they that are upright, shall dwell in the earth; and the simple shall continue in it|Recti habitabunt in terra, et simplices permanebunt in ea]] [the margin gives Prov. iii, 21; the words are Prov 2:21]; and again: God's [[Prov 3:32|communication is with the simple|Cum simplicibus sermocinatio Dei]]. To this simplicity James exhorts, saying: [[Jas 4:8|purify your hearts, ye double minded|Purificate corda, duplices animo]]. Further, that we have behaved thus towards you is clear:

paras.t: Non enim alia, id est opposita, scribimus vobis in hac secunda epistola, quam quæ legistis in prima epistola vobis a me missa, et cognovistis ex lectione illius epistolæ, imo et per experientiam operum meorum inter vos. Spero autem quod usque in finem, id est perseveranter ac firmiter, cognoscetis nos in simplicitate et sinceritate conversari, sicut et cognovistis nos ex parte, id est, quemadmodum partim jam rectitudinem nostram considerastis expertique estis ; quia gloria vestra, id est causa vestræ lætitiæ, nos sumus. Honestus enim et sapiens pater lætificat filios bonos, qui utique in gratia patris sui cordialiter jucundantur. Simul et vos estis gloria nostra. Nam filius sapiens, gloria est patris, ut Salomon dicit. Maxime enim gaudent boni patres de filiorum studiorum profectu, sicut Joannes in sua Canonica : Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare. Unde alio loco dicit Apostolus : Nunc vivimus, si vos statis in Domino. Sic autem unus nostrum est gloria alterius in die Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est ad hoc, ut in die judicii simul glorificemur. Vel, quod unus sit gloria alterius, evidentius apparebit in die prædicto, quando omnia aperta erunt ac nuda : propter quod, tempus illud dies vocatur.
paras.en: [[1:13|For we write no other things to you|Non enim alia scribimus vobis]] (other, that is, contrary) in this second epistle, [[1:13|than what you have read|quam quæ legistis]] in the first epistle sent you by me, [[1:13|and known|et cognovistis]] from the reading of that epistle, and indeed from experience of my works among you. [[1:13|And I hope that you shall know unto the end|Spero autem quod usque in finem]], that is, perseveringly and firmly, you shall know us to live in simplicity and sincerity, [[1:14|As also you have known us in part|sicut et cognovistis nos ex parte]], that is, as you have already in part observed and experienced our uprightness; [[1:14|that we are your glory|quia gloria vestra]], that is, the cause of your joy. For an honourable and wise father gladdens good sons, who indeed rejoice from the heart in their father's favour. [[1:14|as you also are ours|Simul et vos estis gloria nostra]]. For a wise son is the glory of his father, as Solomon says [no verse has these exact words; compare Prov 10:1, "A wise son maketh the father glad", and Prov 17:6]. For good fathers rejoice most of all at the progress of their sons in their studies, as John in his canonical epistle: [[3 John 1:4|I have no greater grace than this, to hear that my children walk in truth|Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulare]]. Hence the Apostle says in another place: [[1 Thess 3:8|now we live, if you stand in the Lord|Nunc vivimus, si vos statis in Domino]]. So, then, each of us is the glory of the other [[1:14|in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ|in die Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, to this end, that we may be glorified together in the day of judgement. Or: that each is the glory of the other will appear more plainly on that day, when all things will be open and naked[[Heb 4:13||]]: on which account that time is called a day.

paras.t: Et hac confidentia, qua ita sincere me circa vos habui, et quia unus nostrum alterius est gloria, volui prius venire ad vos quam ire in Macedoniam, sicut promisi me venturum ad vos : quamvis ita non feci propter culpam vestram, scilicet propter vestram perversitatem et litem ; ut secundam gratiam, id est alium profectum, haberetis ex meo adventu, qui infructuosus non est, hoc est, ut sicut in primo adventu meo ad vos, instruxi vos circa credenda, sic modo docerem vos circa agenda ; et per vos, id est a vobis, et vestro ducatu, transire in Macedoniam, provinciam Græciæ ; et iterum a Macedonia volui venire ad vos, ut tertiam gratiam, id est, perfectam informationem haberetis, et a vobis deduci in Judæam, ut sanctis qui ibi sunt, vestras eleemosynas ferrem. Sed quia Apostolus non venit sicut prædixit, quidam Corinthiorum reprehenderunt ipsum de levitate, falsitate et carnalitate, quasi propter corporale commodum venire distulerit. Ideo de iis malis se excusans, adjecit :
paras.en: [[1:15|And in this confidence|Et hac confidentia]], with which I bore myself so sincerely towards you, and because each of us is the glory of the other, [[1:15|I had a mind to come to you before|volui prius venire ad vos]] going into Macedonia, as I promised that I would come to you[[1 Cor 16:5||]]: though I did not do so, because of your fault, namely because of your perversity and strife; [[1:15|that you might have a second grace|ut secundam gratiam]], that is, a further progress, from my coming, which is not fruitless: that is, that as at my first coming to you I instructed you about what is to be believed, so now I might teach you about what is to be done; [[1:16|And to pass by you into Macedonia|et per vos transire in Macedoniam]] (by you, that is, from you, and under your escort), a province of Greece; [[1:16|and again from Macedonia to come to you|et iterum a Macedonia volui venire ad vos]], that you might have a third grace, that is, a complete formation, [[1:16|and by you to be brought on my way towards Judea|et a vobis deduci in Judæam]], to carry your alms to the saints who are there. But because the Apostle did not come as he had foretold, some of the Corinthians blamed him for fickleness, falsehood and carnality, as though he had put off coming for the sake of some bodily convenience. Therefore, excusing himself of these faults, he added:

paras.t: Quum ergo hoc cogitavi, id est, vos visitare optassem, sicut jam dixi, numquid levitate aut instabilitate usus sum, mutando propositum sine rationabili causa? aut quæ cogito, secundum carnem cogito? id est, numquid carnali sensu utor, dum vos visitare propono, quod tamen non facio, tanquam propter carnis commoditatem hoc differam, ut sit apud me Est et Non, id est affirmatio et negatio de eodem, puta mendacium? Non utique, quoniam nihil dixi intentione fallendi : et hoc ipsum quod dixi, intelligendum erat, nisi rationabile impedimentum occurreret. Mendacium vero est falsa vocis significatio cum intentione fallendi.
paras.en: [[1:17|Whereas then I was thus minded|Quum ergo hoc cogitavi]], that is, had wished to visit you, as I have just said, [[1:17|did I use lightness|numquid levitate]] or inconstancy, changing my purpose without reasonable cause? [[1:17|Or, the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh|aut quæ cogito, secundum carnem cogito]]? that is, do I follow a fleshly mind when I propose to visit you and yet do not do it, as though I were putting it off for the sake of bodily convenience, [[1:17|that there should be with me, It is, and It is not|ut sit apud me Est et Non]], that is, affirmation and denial of the same thing, in a word a lie? Surely not, since I said nothing with intent to deceive: and what I said was to be understood as holding unless some reasonable hindrance arose. For a lie is a false signification of the voice with intent to deceive.

paras.t: Fidelis autem, id est verus in promissis, Deus est : idcirco non mittit nuntios falsos et infideles. Cujus signum vel ratio est : quia sermo noster qui fuit apud vos, id est prædicatio nostra vobis proposita, non est in illo Est et Non, id est affirmans et negans aliquid de eodem secundum idem, sic enim mendax esset ; sed est in illo Est, id est, simpliciter affirmavit esse in Deo, vel in effectibus ejus, quod in eis est, id est quod eis veraciter competit.
paras.en: [[1:18|But God is faithful|Fidelis autem Deus]], that is, true in his promises: therefore he does not send false and faithless messengers. The sign or reason of this is: [[1:18|for our preaching which was to you|quia sermo noster qui fuit apud vos]], that is, our preaching set before you, [[1:18|was not, It is, and It is not|non est in illo Est et Non]], that is, affirming and denying something of the same thing in the same respect, for so it would be lying; but in it there is "It is", that is, it simply affirmed to be in God, or in his effects, what is in them, that is, what truly belongs to them.

paras.t: Dei enim Filius Jesus Christus, qui in vobis per nos prædicatus est, id est a nobis vobis evangelizatus, videlicet per me sicut per principalem, et Silvanum (quem aliqui dicunt esse Silam apostolum) et Timotheum, cooperatores adjutoresque meos, non fuit in illo Est et Non est, id est contradictionem includens seu falsitatem : sed Est in illo fuit, id est, sermo noster de Christo sic pronuntiatus est, sicut vere in Christo impletum est. Vere enim natus, passus ac resuscitatus est, sicut docuimus.
paras.en: [[1:19|For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us|Dei enim Filius Jesus Christus, qui in vobis per nos prædicatus est]], that is, preached to you as the gospel by us, namely [[1:19|by me|per me]] as the principal, [[1:19|and Sylvanus|et Silvanum]] (whom some say is Silas the apostle) [[1:19|and Timothy|et Timotheum]], my fellow workers and helpers, [[1:19|was not: It is and It is not|non fuit in illo Est et Non est]], that is, including contradiction or falsehood: [[1:19|But, It is, was in him|sed Est in illo fuit]], that is, our word about Christ was pronounced just as it was truly fulfilled in Christ. For he was truly born, suffered and rose again, as we taught.

paras.t: Quotquot enim promissiones Dei sunt, id est universæ promissiones Patris factæ de Christo, in illo etiam Est, id est, in Christo vere implentur. Unde Joannes dicit : Gratia et veritas per Christum facta est. Et Christus in cruce dicebat : Consummatum est. Ideo dicimus et per ipsum Christum, Amen, id est, verum est, Deo Patri, quia per Christum fatemur verificata esse Patris promissa, ad gloriam nostram, id est ad nostram salutem, quæ consistit in hoc quod divinam veritatem agnoscimus atque fatemur, sicut ait Salvator : Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo.
paras.en: [[1:20|For all the promises of God are|Quotquot enim promissiones Dei sunt]], that is, all the promises of the Father made concerning Christ, [[1:20|in him, It is|in illo etiam Est]], that is, they are truly fulfilled in Christ. Hence John says: [[John 1:17|grace and truth came by Jesus Christ|Gratia et veritas per Christum facta est]]. And Christ on the cross said: [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]]. [[1:20|Therefore also by him, amen|Ideo dicimus et per ipsum Christum, Amen]], we say (that is, it is true), [[1:20|to God|Deo Patri]] the Father, because through Christ we confess that the Father's promises have been made true, [[1:20|unto our glory|ad gloriam nostram]], that is, unto our salvation, which consists in this, that we acknowledge and confess the divine truth, as the Saviour says: He that [[Matt 10:32|shall confess me before men, I will also confess him before my Father|Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo]][[Luke 12:8||]].

paras.t: Qui autem confirmat nos vobiscum, id est nos et vos simul, in Christo, id est in fide et dilectione Christi, et qui unxit nos interna et spirituali unctione, videlicet perfusione Spiritus Sancti : de qua et apostolus Joannes : Vos unctionem habetis a Sancto ; et unctio ejus docet vos de omnibus. Hæc unctio primo confertur in Baptismo. Qui ergo sic confirmavit et unxit nos, est Deus : qui et signavit nos, id est, in libro vitæ conscripsit, ab aliis discrevit, et ad se pertinere monstravit, et dedit pignus Spiritus, id est arrham Spiritus Sancti, videlicet dona divina, quæ sunt pignus certificans nos de inhabitatione Spiritus Sancti, et futura beatitudine nobis præstanda. Ex perceptione quippe præsentium munerum, certa fit expectatio futurorum. Itaque, qui dedit pignus istud in cordibus nostris, in quibus dona Spiritus Sancti recipiuntur, est Deus. Ideo omne bonum ei adscribimus.
paras.en: [[1:21|Now he that confirmeth us with you|Qui autem confirmat nos vobiscum]], that is, us and you together, [[1:21|in Christ|in Christo]], that is, in the faith and love of Christ, [[1:21|and that hath anointed us|et qui unxit nos]] with an inward and spiritual anointing, namely the outpouring of the Holy Ghost: of which the apostle John also speaks: [[1 John 2:20|you have the unction from the Holy One|Vos unctionem habetis a Sancto]]; and [[1 John 2:27|his unction teacheth you of all things|unctio ejus docet vos de omnibus]]. This anointing is first bestowed in Baptism. He then who has thus confirmed and anointed us [[1:21|is God|est Deus]]: [[1:22|Who also hath sealed us|qui et signavit nos]], that is, has written us in the book of life, set us apart from others, and shown that we belong to him, [[1:22|and given the pledge of the Spirit|et dedit pignus Spiritus]], that is, the earnest of the Holy Ghost, namely the divine gifts, which are a pledge assuring us of the indwelling of the Holy Ghost and of the beatitude to be granted us hereafter. For from receiving the present gifts the expectation of those to come is made certain. So he who gave this pledge [[1:22|in our hearts|in cordibus nostris]], in which the gifts of the Holy Ghost are received, is God. Therefore we ascribe every good to him.

paras.t: Insuper pandit cur ad eos non venerit : Ego autem testem Deum invoco, id est, per Deum testor et juro : et hoc, in animam meam, id est contra bonum animæ meæ, si mentior ; quod parcens vobis, id est, vestræ infirmitati condescendens ac providens, non veni ultra, id est post primam vicem, vel a tempore ultimi recessus mei a vobis, Corinthum, videlicet ne cogerer vehementer dure corripere vos : ideo malui vos scripto corrigere, vobisque aliquantum correctis, venire.
paras.en: Further, he makes plain why he did not come to them: [[1:23|But I call God to witness|Ego autem testem Deum invoco]], that is, I testify and swear by God: and this [[1:23|upon my soul|in animam meam]], that is, against the good of my soul, if I lie; [[1:23|that to spare you|quod parcens vobis]], that is, condescending to your weakness and providing for it, [[1:23|I came not any more|non veni ultra]], that is, after the first time, or since my last departure from you, [[1:23|to Corinth|Corinthum]]: namely, lest I should be forced to rebuke you very harshly; so I preferred to correct you by writing, and to come when you had been somewhat corrected.

paras.t: Non quia dominamur fidei vestræ, id est vobis fidelibus. Tanquam dicat : Non ideo assero me vobis pepercisse, quasi fides vestra nostro subjiciatur imperio, quum fides sit voluntatis, vel quasi vobis dominemur. Unde Petrus : Pascite, inquit, qui in vobis est gregem, non ut dominantes in cleris, sed forma gregis effecti. Sed adjutores, id est cooperatores, sumus gaudii vestri spiritualis, quod nunc habetis per fidem, et in futuro sortituri estis per speciem : hoc est, inducimus vos per exhortationem ad opera bona, ex quibus gloriamini in Domino jam in isto exsilio, et per quæ futuram felicitatem meremini : de qua Salvator, Intra, inquit, in gaudium Domini tui. Adjutores, inquam, sumus gaudii vestri, idcirco, nam fide statis : id est, per fidem erecti estis ad Deum in bonis operibus, ideo cooperamur vobis, inducendo vos ad perseverantiam atque profectum.
paras.en: [[1:23|not because we exercise dominion over your faith|Non quia dominamur fidei vestræ]], that is, over you the faithful. As if he said: I do not say that I spared you on the ground that your faith is subject to our command (since faith is a matter of the will), or as though we lorded it over you. Hence Peter: [[1 Pet 5:2|Feed|Pascite]], he says, the flock [[1 Pet 5:2|which is among you|qui in vobis est gregem]], not [[1 Pet 5:3|as lording it over the clergy but being made a pattern of the flock|ut dominantes in cleris, sed forma gregis effecti]]. [[1:23|but we are helpers|Sed adjutores]], that is, fellow workers, [[1:23|of your joy|sumus gaudii vestri]], the spiritual joy which you now have by faith, and will obtain in the future by sight: that is, we lead you by exhortation to good works, in which you glory in the Lord already in this exile, and by which you merit the happiness to come, of which the Saviour says: [[Matt 25:21|Enter thou|Intra]], he says, [[Matt 25:21|into the joy of thy lord|in gaudium Domini tui]]. [[1:23|we are helpers|Adjutores]], I say, [[1:23|of your joy|sumus gaudii vestri]], for this reason: [[1:23|For in faith you stand|nam fide statis]]: that is, by faith you are raised up to God in good works; therefore we work together with you, leading you on to perseverance and progress.

2.title: Explanatio capituli secundi: Statui autem hoc apud me, etc.
2.title_en: Explanation of the second chapter: But I determined this with myself

paras.t: Denique plenius reserans Apostolus cur ad Corinthios ultra non venerit, ait: Statui autem hoc apud me, id est, in animo meo firmiter ordinavi atque proposui, ne iterum in tristitia, id est cum cordis dolore, venirem ad vos, dolendo propter vestram discordiam. Vel, In tristitia, id est, ne veniens vos tristes efficerem, corripiendo vos dure: doleo namque de vestra imperfectione. Quod patet per hoc: Si enim ego contristo vos, redarguendo vestra peccata; et quis ex vobis est qui me lætificet, id est, tristitiam meam in lætitiam mutet, nisi qui contristatur, id est, ad bonam tristitiam, scilicet pœnitentiam salutarem, movetur, ex me, id est ex mea increpatione? Quemadmodum ergo de vestris culpis doleo, ita de pœnitentia vestra exsulto. Et hoc ipsum, videlicet quod nemo errantium in vobis me lætificat, nisi qui contristatur ex me, scripsi vobis in ista epistola, ut non, quum venero ad vos, tristitiam novam super tristitiam ante conceptam habeam, id est, ne vehementer doleam inveniendo vos in dissensionibus constitutos; de quibus, id est de quorum profectu atque salute, oportuerat, id est, decens erat, me gaudere in Domino, eo quod sum confidens in omnibus vobis, id est, de vestra correctione et obedientia præsumo et spero, quia meum gaudium spirituale, quo de vestra emendatione et gratia lætor, omnium vestrum est, id est, in vos redundat, vobisque prodest atque commune est. Sicut enim ego de vestra correctione glorior, sic et vos de eadem gloriari debetis.
paras.en: Finally, disclosing more fully why he did not come to the Corinthians again, the Apostle says: [[2:1|But I determined this with myself|Statui autem hoc apud me]], that is, I firmly ordained and resolved in my mind, that I would not come [[2:1|again in sorrow|ne iterum in tristitia]], that is, with sorrow of heart, [[2:1|to you|venirem ad vos]] [the Douay-Rheims text reads "to come to you again in sorrow"; the Latin has *ne*, "that I would not come"], grieving on account of your discord. Or, [[2:1|in sorrow|In tristitia]], that is, lest by coming I should make you sorrowful, rebuking you harshly: for I grieve over your imperfection. This is plain from what follows: [[2:2|For if I make you sorrowful|Si enim ego contristo vos]], by reproving your sins, [[2:2|who is he then that can make me glad|et quis ex vobis est qui me lætificet]] (that is, can turn my sorrow into joy) [[2:2|but the same who is made sorrowful|nisi qui contristatur]], that is, is moved to a good sorrow, namely to salutary penance, [[2:2|by me|ex me]], that is, by my rebuke? As therefore I grieve over your faults, so I exult over your penance. [[2:3|And I wrote this same|Et hoc ipsum]], namely that none of those among you who err gladdens me but he who is made sorrowful by me, [[2:3|to you|scripsi vobis]] in this epistle, [[2:3|that I may not, when I come, have sorrow upon sorrow|ut non, quum venero ad vos, tristitiam novam super tristitiam ante conceptam habeam]] (a new sorrow upon the sorrow already conceived), that is, lest I grieve exceedingly in finding you set in dissensions; [[2:3|from them of whom|de quibus]], that is, over whose progress and salvation, [[2:3|I ought|oportuerat]], that is, it was fitting, [[2:3|to rejoice|me gaudere]] in the Lord, since I am [[2:3|having confidence in you all|confidens in omnibus vobis]], that is, I presume upon and hope for your correction and obedience, [[2:3|that my joy|quia meum gaudium]], the spiritual joy with which I rejoice over your amendment and grace, [[2:3|is the joy of you all|omnium vestrum est]], that is, overflows upon you, and profits you, and is common to you. For as I glory in your correction, so you too ought to glory in the same.

paras.t: Habui autem magnam tristitiam, percepta vestra dissensione: cujus signum est: Nam ex multa tribulatione, id est afflictione, et angustia, id est pressura et sollicitudine cordis, scripsi vobis superiorem epistolam, per multas lacrimas, id est copiose lugendo ob vestros errores. Et hoc feci, vel me hoc fecisse jam recito, non finaliter ad hoc ut contristemini: tristitia non est finis ultimate intentus, sed gloria; sed ut sciatis per experientiam […]am curæ meæ ad vos, quam caritatem, id est, quantam […] quamque specialem dilectionem, habeam abundantius, id est multum […]stras personas inter, in vobis, id est ad vestras; hocque scientes, libentius […] admonitionibus meis, certi […]ritate procedant. Nihil enim […] dilectionem, sicut dum unus […]mari ab alio. Hinc etiam co[…]num ac utile sit alii […]manitionem quæ ad ipsum habe[…]manti facilius consentitur. Per […]nen, hoc malum est: primo, […]eciem adulationis; secundo, si […]e moveatur ad gloriam vanam.
paras.en: Now I had great sorrow when I learned of your dissension; and the sign of it is this: [[2:4|For out of much affliction|Nam ex multa tribulatione]], that is, distress, [[2:4|and anguish|et angustia]], that is, oppression and anxiety of heart, [[2:4|I wrote to you|scripsi vobis]] the former epistle, [[2:4|with many tears|per multas lacrimas]], that is, weeping copiously over your errors. And this I did (or, I now recount that I did this) [[2:4|not that you should be made sorrowful|non finaliter ad hoc ut contristemini]] as the final end (sorrow is not the end ultimately intended, but glory), [[2:4|but that you might know|sed ut sciatis]] by experience […] of my care for you, [[2:4|the charity|quam caritatem]], that is, how great […] and how special a love, [[2:4|I have more abundantly|habeam abundantius]], that is, much […] persons […], [[2:4|towards you|in vobis]], that is, towards your own [the Latin here is disordered and damaged: "…stras personas inter, in vobis, id est ad vestras"]; and, knowing this, more willingly […] my admonitions, sure […] proceed. For nothing […] love, as when one […] loved by another. Hence also […] good and useful to another […] admonition which […] is more readily assented to [from "per experientiam" to the end of this paragraph the beginnings of many lines are lost in the source]. […], this is evil: first, […] appearance of flattery; secondly, if […] be moved to vain glory.

paras.t: […]gil Apostolus de illo enormi fornicatore qui patris sui ha[…]m, quem et Apostolus tradidit […]t in prima epistola patuit. Si […] id est aliquis vestrum, cor[…] maxime fornicator præductus, […]ristari tristitia immoderata […]nis impediente: quæ in sapi[…]adit, secundum Philosophum. […]tia scriptum est: Non con[…]tum quidquid ei acciderit; […]istitiam longe expelle a te […]a accidit tristitia, et non est […]a. Itaque. Non me contrista[…] […], id est aliquo[…] […]oderate, prout caritas exigit tristari de peccato alterius. Vel, Non me contristavit, scilicet solum, sed ex parte, id est, etiam aliqui aliorum me contristarunt. Et hoc dico, ut non onerem omnes vos, id est, ne videar omnibus vobis gravem culpam imponere, et increpationem inducere.
paras.en: […] the Apostle […] of that monstrous fornicator who […] of his father[[1 Cor 5:1||]] [the lost words were evidently "had his father's wife"], whom the Apostle also delivered […], as appeared in the first epistle. [[2:5|And if any one|Si]] […], that is, any one of you, […] especially the aforesaid fornicator, […] be made sorrowful with an immoderate sorrow, […] of reason hindering: which […] in the wise man, according to the Philosopher [the sense was evidently that such sorrow does not befall the wise man]. […] it is written: [[Prov 12:21|Whatsoever shall befall the just man, shall not make him sad|quidquid ei acciderit]] [Prov 12:21; the opening words, *Non contristabit justum*, are partly lost here]; […] [[Ecclus 30:24|drive away sadness far from thee|istitiam longe expelle a te]] […] [[Ecclus 30:25|sadness hath killed many, and there is|accidit tristitia, et non est]] […] [*accidit* is printed where the Vulgate has *occidit*, "hath killed"]. Therefore, [[2:5|he hath not grieved me|Non me contrista]] […], that is, in some […] measure, as charity requires one to grieve over another's sin [a word ending in *-oderate* is partly lost, probably *moderate*, "in measure"]. Or, [[2:5|he hath not grieved me|Non me contristavit]], that is, not me alone, [[2:5|but in part|sed ex parte]], that is, some of the others also have grieved me. And this I say [[2:5|that I may not burden you all|ut non onerem omnes vos]], that is, lest I seem to lay a grave fault upon you all and to bring a rebuke upon you.

paras.t: Sufficit illi, id est, satis gravis et pro sufficienti pœna reputanda est, qui ejusmodi est, id est fornicatori præfato, objurgatio hæc, id est increpatio et excommunicatio, quæ fit, id est, facta est illi, a pluribus, id est omnibus vobis, quibus collectis objurgatus fuit. Magnum enim intra se fert tormentum, qui vitia sua cernit ab omnibus detestari. Et in tantum sufficit ei objurgatio ista, ita ut econtrario, scilicet pro excommunicatione, magis donetis ei, id est, ignoscatis, et consolemini eum verbis atque exemplis sacræ Scripturæ ad divinæ misericordiæ commendationem spectantibus: ut est illud in Ezechiele, Nolo mortem peccatoris; et illud Zachariæ, Convertimini ad me, et convertar ad vos, dicit Dominus; ne forte abundantiori tristitia absorbeatur, id est, inordinato mœrore et excessivo cordis dolore desperet et pereat, qui ejusmodi est, id est fornicator jam dictus: quia ut Salomon ait, In mœrore animi dejicitur spiritus.
paras.en: [[2:6|To him|illi]] [[2:6|is sufficient|Sufficit]], that is, it is grave enough and is to be reckoned a sufficient punishment, [[2:6|who is such a one|qui ejusmodi est]], that is, for the aforesaid fornicator, [[2:6|this rebuke|objurgatio hæc]], that is, the reproof and excommunication, [[2:6|which is given|quæ fit]], that is, which has been given him, [[2:6|by many|a pluribus]], that is, by all of you, assembled together, by whom he was rebuked. For he bears a great torment within himself who sees his vices detested by all. And this rebuke suffices him to such a degree, [[2:7|So that on the contrary|ita ut econtrario]], namely instead of excommunication, [[2:7|you should rather forgive him|magis donetis ei]], that is, pardon him, [[2:7|and comfort him|et consolemini]] with words and examples of holy Scripture that serve to commend the divine mercy: such as that in Ezechiel, [[Ezech 33:11|I desire not the death of the wicked|Nolo mortem peccatoris]] [Denis has "of the sinner"; the margin gives Ezech. xxxiii, 32 and xxxiii, 11; the first is probably Ezech 18:32, "I desire not the death of him that dieth"], and that of Zacharias, [[Zach 1:3|Turn ye to me|Convertimini ad me]], [[Zach 1:3|and I will turn to you, saith the Lord|et convertar ad vos, dicit Dominus]]; [[2:7|lest perhaps such a one be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow|ne forte abundantiori tristitia absorbeatur]], that is, despair and perish through inordinate grief and excessive sorrow of heart, [[2:7|such a one|qui ejusmodi est]], that is, the fornicator already mentioned: for, as Solomon says, [[Prov 15:13|by grief of mind the spirit is cast down|In mœrore animi dejicitur spiritus]].

paras.t: Propter quod obsecro vos ex humilitate, qui possem præcipere apostolica auctoritate, ut confirmetis, id est, per opera caritativa ac fortia ostendatis, in illum pœnitentem caritatem fraternam, hortando, consolando, atque ad pristinam societatem et communionem ipsum admittendo. Ideo enim et scripsi vobis, ut cognoscam, id est videam, experimentum vestrum, id est facta experimentalia, per quæ experimentaliter constet, an in omnibus præceptis et admonitionibus obedientes sitis mihi: quatenus, si ita non est, instruam vos plenius de obedientia generaliter observanda. Viris quippe heroicis, divinis atque perfectis, quos certum est a Spiritu Sancto moveri, in omnibus obediendum videtur, etiam si supra vires et contra rationem naturalem videtur quod jubetur.
paras.en: [[2:8|Wherefore, I beseech you|Propter quod obsecro vos]] out of humility, I who could command by apostolic authority, [[2:8|that you would confirm|ut confirmetis]], that is, show by works of charity and of strength, [[2:8|your charity towards him|in illum pœnitentem caritatem]], now penitent, a brotherly charity, by exhorting him, comforting him, and admitting him to his former fellowship and communion. [[2:9|For to this end also did I write|Ideo enim et scripsi vobis]], [[2:9|that I may know|ut cognoscam]], that is, see, [[2:9|the experiment of you|experimentum vestrum]], that is, the deeds of trial by which it may be established by experience [[2:9|whether you be obedient in all things|an in omnibus præceptis et admonitionibus obedientes sitis]], in all my precepts and admonitions, to me: so that, if it is not so, I may instruct you more fully about the obedience to be observed in general. For heroic men, divine and perfect, who are certainly moved by the Holy Ghost, ought, it seems, to be obeyed in all things, even if what is commanded seems beyond one's strength and against natural reason.

paras.t: Cur vero donare et parcere debeant prædicto pœnitenti, quem Apostolus non exprimit nominatim, ne confundatur, subjungitur: Cui autem aliquid donastis, id est ei cui vos ignovistis, et ego donavi. Nam quum illi rogabant Apostolum pro indulgentia et reconciliatione alicujus injusti, Apostolus consensit: ideo dignum est ut et ipsi quoque ignoscant pro quo rogat Apostolus, et ut donatio seu remissio Apostoli agnoscatur rata et efficax. Nam et ego donavi, id est, ignovi, et absolvi pœnitentem, si quid donavi (hoc addit Apostolus, ad innuendum quod non passim aut indiscrete donavit, sicut et Timotheo transcripsit: Manus cito nemini imposueris), propter vos, id est ad vestram instantiam. Hoc feci in persona Christi, id est vice et loco Christi, cujus vicarii sumus: quibus et ipse suam potestatem commisit, et solvendi itemque ligandi virtutem largitus est; ut non circumveniamur a Satana, id est, ne a diabolo decipiamur, habendo nos nimium rigorose aut nimis remisse circa subjectos: quorum utrumque prælato vitandum est. Non enim ignoramus cogitationes ejus in communi, id est machinamenta, astutias atque suggestiones, quibus conatur fideles a medio virtutis retrahere. In speciali tamen nescit aliquis cogitationes dæmonum, sicut nec hominum, nisi ex speciali revelatione.
paras.en: But why they ought to pardon and spare the aforesaid penitent (whom the Apostle does not name, lest he be put to shame) is added: [[2:10|And to whom you have pardoned any thing|Cui autem aliquid donastis]], that is, him whom you have forgiven, [[2:10|I also|et ego donavi]] have pardoned. For when they were asking the Apostle for the pardon and reconciliation of some wrongdoer, the Apostle consented: therefore it is fitting that they too should forgive the one for whom the Apostle asks, and that the Apostle's pardon or remission should be acknowledged as ratified and effectual. [[2:10|For, what I have pardoned|Nam et ego donavi]], that is, I have forgiven and absolved the penitent, [[2:10|if I have pardoned any thing|si quid donavi]] (this the Apostle adds to hint that he did not pardon at random or without discretion, as he also wrote to Timothy: [[1 Tim 5:22|Impose not hands lightly upon any man|Manus cito nemini imposueris]]), [[2:10|for your sakes|propter vos]], that is, at your instance, [[2:10|have I done it in the person of Christ|Hoc feci in persona Christi]], that is, in the stead and place of Christ, whose vicars we are: to whom He has also committed His power, and bestowed the power of loosing and likewise of binding[[Matt 16:19||]][[Matt 18:18||]]; [[2:11|That we be not overreached by Satan|ut non circumveniamur a Satana]], that is, lest we be deceived by the devil, by bearing ourselves too rigorously or too leniently towards our subjects: both of which a prelate must avoid. [[2:11|For we are not ignorant of his devices|Non enim ignoramus cogitationes ejus]] in general, that is, his machinations, cunning and suggestions, by which he tries to draw the faithful back from the mean of virtue. In particular, however, no one knows the thoughts of demons [*cogitationes*, the word rendered "devices" above], as neither those of men, except by special revelation.

paras.t: Præterea manifestat Apostolus, quod occasione Corinthiorum impeditus sit Troade. Quum autem venissem Troadem propter Evangelium Christi illic prædicandum, et ostium mihi apertum esset, id est corda hominum aperta et præparata recipere verbum Dei, in Domino, id est in virtute et gratia Dei; vel, In Domino, id est secundum placitum voluntatis divinæ; non habui requiem spiritui meo, id est, mente quietus non fui, nec desiderio meo satisfacere potui, eo quod non invenerim ibi Titum fratrem meum, episcopum Cretensem, sicut condixeramus. Impeditus enim Titus et retardatus, mansit apud Corinthios. Unde eo absente non potuit Apostolus et adversariis resistere, et fideles satis instruere. Sed valefaciens eis, videlicet Trojanis conversis, profectus sum in Macedoniam. Ad quod forsitan pertinet illud Actuum: Quum autem pertransissent Mysiam, descenderunt Troadem; et visio per noctem Paulo ostensa est: Vir Macedo quidam erat stans et deprecans eum, et dicens: Transiens in Macedoniam, adjuva nos.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle shows that he was held back at Troas on account of the Corinthians. [[2:12|And when I was come to Troas for the gospel of Christ|Quum autem venissem Troadem propter Evangelium Christi]], to preach it there, [[2:12|and a door was opened unto me|et ostium mihi apertum esset]], that is, men's hearts were open and prepared to receive the word of God, [[2:12|in the Lord|in Domino]], that is, in the power and grace of God; or, [[2:12|in the Lord|In Domino]], that is, according to the good pleasure of the divine will; [[2:13|I had no rest in my spirit|non habui requiem spiritui meo]], that is, I was not quiet in mind, nor could I satisfy my desire, [[2:13|because I found not Titus my brother|eo quod non invenerim ibi Titum fratrem meum]] there, the bishop of Crete, as we had agreed. For Titus, hindered and delayed, stayed with the Corinthians. Hence, in his absence, the Apostle could not both resist the adversaries and instruct the faithful sufficiently. [[2:13|but bidding them farewell|Sed valefaciens eis]], namely the converted Trojans [that is, the people of Troas], [[2:13|I went into Macedonia|profectus sum in Macedoniam]]. To this perhaps belongs that passage of the Acts: [[Acts 16:8|And when they had passed through Mysia, they went down to Troas|Quum autem pertransissent Mysiam, descenderunt Troadem]]; [[Acts 16:9|And a vision was shewed to Paul in the night, which was a man of Macedonia standing and beseeching him and saying: Pass over into Macedonia and help us|et visio per noctem Paulo ostensa est: Vir Macedo quidam erat stans et deprecans eum, et dicens: Transiens in Macedoniam, adjuva nos]].

paras.t: Incipit insuper Apostolus commendare se ipsum, propter causas superius assignatas. Deo autem gratias referimus, qui semper triumphat, id est triumphare facit, nos in Christo Jesu, id est in virtute et gratia Christi; et odorem notitiæ suæ, id est dulcem ac odoriferam suæ majestatis sapientiam, id est sacræ Scripturæ doctrinam (quæ dulcis est, quia inflammat affectum: quod non facit naturalis sapientia, nisi debili modo), manifestat per nos, id est per nostram prædicationem, in omni loco: quemadmodum scriptum est, In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum.
paras.en: Moreover, the Apostle begins to commend himself, for the reasons given above [the margin here gives I Cor. i, 14, which does not fit; perhaps the verse number 14 of this chapter misread]. [[2:14|Now thanks be to God|Deo autem gratias referimus]] (we give), [[2:14|who always maketh us to triumph|qui semper triumphat]], that is, causes to triumph, [[2:14|in Christ Jesus|nos in Christo Jesu]], that is, in the power and grace of Christ; [[2:14|the odour of his knowledge|et odorem notitiæ suæ]], that is, the sweet and fragrant wisdom of His majesty, that is, the doctrine of holy Scripture (which is sweet because it inflames the affections, which natural wisdom does not do, except in a weak way), [[2:14|and manifesteth|manifestat]] [[2:14|by us|per nos]], that is, through our preaching, [[2:14|in every place|in omni loco]]: as it is written, [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]].

paras.t: Quia Christi bonus odor sumus, id est, per nos, videlicet per nostræ prædicationis instantiam, operationem miraculosam, et conversationem exemplarem, Christi bonitas, veritas atque dulcedo aliis innotescit ac sapit. De tali odore in Canticis legitur: Curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum; itemque, Odor oris tui, sicut odor malorum punicorum. Sic ergo sumus bonus odor Christi Deo, id est ad gloriam sanctæ et superbeatissimæ Trinitatis, cujus fides et gloria mundo per nos revelatur, in his qui salvi fiunt, et in his qui pereunt, sed differenter: aliis quidem, videlicet reprobis, sumus odor mortis culpæ in mortem pœnæ æternæ; per accidens tamen, ratione perversitatis eorum, quia ex nostra prædicatione et bonitate ad invidiam incitantur, graviusque delinquunt; aliis autem, puta electis, sumus odor vitæ gratiæ tendentis in vitam gloriæ, quia ex nostra prædicatione divino accenduntur amore, quo nihil est dulcius.
paras.en: [[2:15|For we are the good odour of Christ|Quia Christi bonus odor sumus]], that is, through us, namely through the urgency of our preaching, our miraculous working and our exemplary conduct, the goodness, truth and sweetness of Christ become known to others and are tasted by them. Of such an odour we read in the Canticles: [[Cant 1:3|we will run after thee to the odour of thy ointments|Curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum]] [the margin gives Cant. i, 4; in the Vulgate numbering used here it is Cant 1:3]; and again, [[Cant 7:8|the odour of thy mouth like apples|Odor oris tui, sicut odor malorum punicorum]] [Denis reads *malorum punicorum*, "of pomegranates"]. So, then, we are the good odour of Christ [[2:15|unto God|Deo]], that is, to the glory of the holy and most supremely blessed Trinity, whose faith and glory are revealed to the world through us, [[2:15|in them that are saved and in them that perish|in his qui salvi fiunt, et in his qui pereunt]], but in different ways: [[2:16|To the one indeed|aliis quidem]], namely the reprobate, we are [[2:16|the odour of death|odor mortis]], the death of guilt, [[2:16|unto death|in mortem]], the death of eternal punishment; this, however, accidentally [that is, not by our own nature or intent, but as a by-product], by reason of their perversity, because they are stirred to envy by our preaching and goodness, and sin more grievously; [[2:16|but to the others|aliis autem]], the elect, for instance, we are [[2:16|the odour of life|odor vitæ]], the life of grace, tending [[2:16|unto life|in vitam]], the life of glory, because by our preaching they are kindled with divine love, than which nothing is sweeter.

paras.t: Et ad hæc agenda, videlicet ut sit aliquis bonus odor Christi, secundum modum dictum, quis illorum pseudoapostolorum tam idoneus est sicut nos Apostoli? Nemo utique. Non enim sumus sicut plurimi falsi doctores, adulterantes verbum Dei, id est perverse interpretantes, et sine fructu debito facientes divinam Scripturam; sed ex sinceritate, id est, pura intentione et vero intellectu verba divina prædicamus, sicut ex Deo edocti, tanquam divinitus informati, et loquentes coram Deo, id est reverenter et sancte, ac si Deum cerneremus præsentem, cujus præsentiam oculo intellectuali attendimus, in Christo, id est secundum Christi voluntatem et institutionem, loquimur.
paras.en: [[2:16|And for these things|Et ad hæc agenda]] (to be done), namely that one should be a good odour of Christ in the manner described, which of those false apostles [[2:16|is so sufficient|tam idoneus est]] as we Apostles? Surely none. [[2:17|For we are not as many|Non enim sumus sicut plurimi]] false teachers, [[2:17|adulterating the word of God|adulterantes verbum Dei]], that is, interpreting it perversely, and making the divine Scripture bear no due fruit; [[2:17|but with sincerity|sed ex sinceritate]], that is, with pure intention and true understanding, we preach the divine words, [[2:17|as from God|sicut ex Deo]] taught, as being divinely instructed, and speaking [[2:17|before God|coram Deo]], that is, reverently and holily, as if we saw God present, whose presence we attend to with the eye of the intellect, [[2:17|in Christ|in Christo]], that is, according to the will and institution of Christ, [[2:17|we speak|loquimur]].

3.title: Declaratio capituli tertii: Incipimus, etc.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: Do we begin, etc.

paras.t: MANIFESTATUM erat Apostolo, quod aliqui Corinthiorum scandalizabantur in hoc quod toties commendavit se ipsum, quasi inaniter moveretur, propriam magis quam Dei gloriam quaerens, quod est contra Salomonis doctrinam, dicentis : Laudet te alienus, et non os tuum ; extraneus, et non labia tua. Unde et Salvator : Si ego glorifico me ipsum, gloria mea nihil est. Ideo Apostolus in hujus capitis exordio excludit malam suspicionem illorum, dicendo : Incipimus iterum in hac epistola, sicut in prima, commendare, id est laudare, nos ipsos, videlicet propter propriam gloriam nostram, et non potius propter gloriam Dei, ad vestri instructionem, ut agnita veritate nobis credatis, non pseudoapostolis? Aut numquid egemus, sicut quidam fallaces atque hypocritæ, commendaticiis, id est laudatoriis, epistolis mittendis ad vos, aut ex vobis, id est a vobis ad alios transmittendis? quasi dicat : Nequaquam indigemus hujusmodi epistolis ex parte nostri, quem propria virtus satis commendat; tamen propter ignaros necessarium est, ne fallantur.
paras.en: It was made known to the Apostle that some of the Corinthians were scandalized at his having commended himself so often, as though he were moved by vanity, seeking his own glory rather than God's; which is against the teaching of Solomon, who says: [[Prov 27:2|Let another praise thee, and not thy own mouth: a stranger, and not thy own lips.|Laudet te alienus, et non os tuum ; extraneus, et non labia tua]] And so too the Saviour: [[John 8:54|If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing|Si ego glorifico me ipsum, gloria mea nihil est]].
