Sive sobrii sumus, moderate loquendo de perfectionibus nostris, sicut ad virtuosum sapientemque pertinet, ut in his quæ propriam laudem concernunt, magis declinet ad minus quam ad majus; vobis, id est, pro vestri informatione et commodo hoc facimus.
paras.en: Or thus: [[5:13|whether we be transported in mind|Sive mente excedimus]], that is, if in praising ourselves we seem to be out of our senses (for it belongs to fools to dwell on their own praises), [[5:13|it is to God|Deo]], that is, we do this for the glory of God, that God may be blessed in his gifts. [[5:13|or whether we be sober|Sive sobrii sumus]], speaking with moderation of our perfections, as befits a virtuous and wise man, so that in what concerns his own praise he leans rather to less than to more, [[5:13|it is for you|vobis]], that is, we do this for your instruction and profit.

paras.t: Caritas enim Christi, id est dilectio qua Christum proximumque diligimus, urget, id est, incitat et vehementer inclinat, nos ista efficere, quoniam Christi gloriam et proximorum salutem tanto amplius zelamus, quanto in vera caritate perfectiores fuerimus; æstimantes, id est firmiter reputantes, hoc, quoniam si (pro quia) unus, utpote solus Christus, pro omnibus hominibus liberandis mortuus est, ergo omnes mortui sunt, id est vitiis mortificati merito passionis Christi, quantum est ex parte ipsius Salvatoris, qui moriendo omnia ad se traxit. Vel, Omnes mortui sunt, id est, mortem culpæ incurrerunt ex originali peccato: aliter non egerent salvatore. Et pro omnibus mortuus est Christus, ut et qui vivunt vita naturæ seu gratiæ, jam non sibi vivant, id est, non propriæ voluntati deserviant, videlicet ad honorem proprium vitam suam ordinent; sed ei vivant, id est, ad ejus honorem et gloriam omnia opera sua interiora exterioraque referant, qui pro ipsis mortuus est et resurrexit, videlicet Christi. Sic vivere Christo, est vere abnegare atque vivifice mortificare se ipsum.
paras.en: [[5:14|For the charity of Christ|Caritas enim Christi]], that is, the love with which we love Christ and our neighbour, [[5:14|presseth|urget]], that is, incites and strongly inclines, us to do these things, since we are the more zealous for the glory of Christ and the salvation of our neighbours the more perfect we are in true charity; [[5:14|judging|æstimantes]], that is, firmly reckoning, [[5:14|this, that if|hoc, quoniam si]] (*if* standing for *since*) [[5:14|one|unus]], namely Christ alone, [[5:14|died for all|pro omnibus hominibus liberandis mortuus est]] men, to set them free, [[5:14|then all were dead|ergo omnes mortui sunt]], that is, mortified to vices by the merit of Christ's passion, so far as lies with the Saviour himself, who by dying drew all things to himself. Or: All were dead, that is, incurred the death of guilt from original sin: otherwise they would not need a saviour. [[5:15|And Christ died for all|Et pro omnibus mortuus est Christus]], [[5:15|that they also who live|ut et qui vivunt]] the life of nature or of grace, [[5:15|may not now live to themselves|jam non sibi vivant]], that is, may not serve their own will, namely by ordering their life to their own honour; [[5:15|but unto him|sed ei vivant]], that is, may refer all their works, inward and outward, to his honour and glory, [[5:15|who died for them and rose again|qui pro ipsis mortuus est et resurrexit]], namely Christ. To live thus to Christ is truly to deny oneself and to mortify oneself unto life.

paras.t: Itaque, id est, quia pro omnibus mortuus est Christus, nos Apostoli et viri perfecti, ex hoc, id est posthac, neminem novimus notitia approbationis, id est, nullum viatorem laudamus, secundum carnem, id est carnaliter, scilicet propter causas indignas. Vel, Neminem novimus secundum carnem, id est secundum ea quæ carnis conditionem respiciunt: talia enim non curamus neque attendimus. Et si cognovimus secundum carnem Christum, id est, quamvis mysteria Christi carnaliter et superficialiter intellexerimus et Christum non nisi secundum humanam naturam noverimus sensu humano, sed nunc jam Spiritu Sancto recepto non novimus eum hoc modo, sed spiritualiter ac supernaturaliter, tanquam Deum et hominem.
paras.en: [[5:16|Wherefore|Itaque]], that is, because Christ died for all, we Apostles and perfect men [[5:16|henceforth|ex hoc]], that is, from now on, [[5:16|we know no man|neminem novimus]] with the knowledge of approval, that is, we praise no wayfarer [that is, no one still on the way, in this life], [[5:16|according to the flesh|secundum carnem]], that is, carnally, namely for unworthy reasons. Or: We know no man according to the flesh, that is, according to the things that regard the condition of the flesh: for such things we do not care for or attend to. [[5:16|And if we have known Christ according to the flesh|Et si cognovimus secundum carnem Christum]], that is, although we understood the mysteries of Christ carnally and superficially, and knew Christ, with human sense, only according to his human nature, [[5:16|but now|sed nunc jam]], having received the Holy Ghost, [[5:16|we know him so no longer|non novimus eum hoc modo]], but spiritually and supernaturally, as God and man.

paras.t: Si quis ergo, id est quia aliqua, in Christo est nova creatura, id est, aliquis in Christi Baptismo renatus est, vetera transierunt, id est, pristina vitia ab illo remota sunt, pœnalitates quoque deletæ sunt modo in spe, tandem delendæ in re; ecce facta sunt omnia nova, id est, per infusionem Spiritus Sancti omnia spiritualiter renovata sunt, corpus, anima, cogitatio, verbum et opera. Unde in Apocalypsi dicitur: Dixit qui sedebat in throno, Ecce nova facio omnia.
paras.en: [[5:17|If then any be|Si quis ergo]], that is, since any one, [[5:17|in Christ|in Christo]] is [[5:17|a new creature|nova creatura]], that is, if any one has been reborn in the Baptism of Christ, [[5:17|the old things are passed away|vetera transierunt]], that is, his former vices have been removed from him, and his penalties too have been blotted out, now in hope, to be blotted out at last in reality; [[5:17|Behold all things are made new|ecce facta sunt omnia nova]], that is, through the infusion of the Holy Ghost all things have been spiritually renewed: body, soul, thought, word and works. Hence it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:5|he that sat on the throne, said: Behold, I make all things new|Dixit qui sedebat in throno, Ecce nova facio omnia]].

paras.t: Omnia autem ex Deo Patre vel sancta Trinitate originaliter profluxerunt et condita sunt, qui nos reconciliavit sibi, id est, peccata nostra nobis ignovit, per Christum, id est incarnatione, passione seu merito Christi hominis: imo Christus ut Deus, reconciliavit nos sibi per se ipsum, ut hominem tollem; et dedit nobis ministerium reconciliationis, id est, officium evangelicæ prædicationis, qua ista reconciliatio annuntiatur hominibus, commisit nobis suis vicariis. Quoniam quidem Deus Pater, vel Verbum increatum, imo et Spiritus Sanctus, hoc est Deus Trinitas, erat in Christo homine mundum, id est electos, reconcilians sibi (ut dictum est), non reputans, id est non juste ulciscens, nec in æternum reservans, illis delicta ipsorum originalia aut actualia. Christus namque Agnus Dei omnia tulit peccata. Et posuit in nobis verbum reconciliationis, id est prædicationem pacificationis inter Deum et homines factæ.
paras.en: [[5:18|But all things are|Omnia autem]] [[5:18|of God|ex Deo]] the Father, or the holy Trinity: from him they have flowed forth in their origin and by him they were made; [[5:18|who hath reconciled us to himself|qui nos reconciliavit sibi]], that is, has forgiven us our sins, [[5:18|by Christ|per Christum]], that is, by the incarnation, passion or merit of Christ as man: nay rather, Christ as God reconciled us to himself through himself as man [the Latin here, *ut hominem tollem*, seems to be corrupt]; [[5:18|and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation|et dedit nobis ministerium reconciliationis]], that is, he has committed to us, his vicars, the office of preaching the Gospel, by which this reconciliation is announced to men. [[5:19|For God indeed|Quoniam quidem Deus]] the Father, or the uncreated Word, nay and the Holy Ghost too, that is, God the Trinity, [[5:19|was in Christ|erat in Christo]] the man, [[5:19|reconciling|reconcilians]] [[5:19|the world|mundum]], that is, the elect, [[5:19|to himself|sibi]] (as has been said), [[5:19|not imputing|non reputans]], that is, not justly punishing nor reserving for ever, [[5:19|to them their sins|illis delicta ipsorum]], original or actual. For Christ, the [[John 1:29|Lamb of God|Agnus Dei]], took away all sins. [[5:19|And he hath placed in us the word of reconciliation|Et posuit in nobis verbum reconciliationis]], that is, the preaching of the peace made between God and men.

paras.t: Pro Christo ergo, id est pro Christi amore et gloria, legatione, id est missione, fungimur, quia a Deo missi sumus annuntiare Evangelium Christi, tanquam Deo exhortante corda audientium per nos, id est per prædicationem nostram. Ipse enim loquitur per nos. Obsecramus pro Christo, id est vice, loco, vel amore Christi, reconciliamini Deo, id est, peccata vestra deflete, vitam corrigite, Deo placere contendite.
paras.en: [[5:20|For Christ therefore|Pro Christo ergo]], that is, for the love and glory of Christ, [[5:20|we are ambassadors|legatione fungimur]] [literally 'we discharge an embassy'; Denis glosses *legatione*, 'embassy', as 'mission'], since we have been sent by God to announce the Gospel of Christ[[1 Cor 1:17||]], [[5:20|God as it were exhorting|tanquam Deo exhortante]] the hearts of the hearers [[5:20|by us|per nos]], that is, through our preaching. For he himself speaks through us. [[5:20|we beseech you|Obsecramus]] [[5:20|for Christ|pro Christo]], that is, in the stead, in the place, or for the love of Christ, [[5:20|be reconciled to God|reconciliamini Deo]], that is, bewail your sins, amend your life, strive to please God.

paras.t: Eum qui non noverat peccatum per approbationem vel experientiam, scilicet Christum, Pater pro nobis, id est pro nostra redemptione, peccatum fecit, id est hostiam pro peccato. Sumitur enim hic peccatum pro hostia peccati, sicut et apud Osee, ubi dicitur: Peccata populi mei comedent. Vel sic: Eum qui non noverat peccatum, pro nobis peccatum, id est culpam, fecit. Peccatum enim, præcipue originale, occasio fuit incarnationis passionisque Christi, sicque quodam modo fecit eum hominem. Ut nos efficeremur justitia Dei, id est justificati a Deo, in illo, id est merito Christi.
paras.en: [[5:21|Him, who knew no sin|Eum qui non noverat peccatum]], by approval or by experience, namely Christ, the Father [[5:21|for us|pro nobis]], that is, for our redemption, [[5:21|hath made sin|peccatum fecit]], that is, a victim for sin. For *sin* is taken here for the sacrifice for sin, as also in Osee, where it is said: [[Osee 4:8|They shall eat the sins of my people|Peccata populi mei comedent]] [that is, the sin-offerings]. Or thus: [[5:21|Him, who knew no sin|Eum qui non noverat peccatum]], [[5:21|for us|pro nobis]] [[5:21|sin|peccatum]], that is, guilt, [[5:21|he hath made|fecit]]. For sin, especially original sin, was the occasion of the incarnation and passion of Christ, and so in a certain manner made him man. [[5:21|That we might be made the justice of God|Ut nos efficeremur justitia Dei]], that is, justified by God, [[5:21|in him|in illo]], that is, by the merit of Christ.

6.title: Explanatio capituli sexti: Adjuvantes autem exhortamur
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: And we helping do exhort you
6.note: Text is lost in the transcription at the start of v. 13, and some line-ends at vv. 4–8. Please check against the scan.

paras.t: Recommendatis novi Testamenti mysteriis, jam omnes ad perfectionem invitantur, dicente Apostolo: Adjuvantes autem verbo, operatione, oratione, vestram imbecillitatem; vel, Adjuvantes, id est Christo cooperantes in vestra conversione; exhortamur ne in vacuum, id est, sine fructu et perseverantia, gratiam Dei habitualem et gratum facientem recipiatis in Baptismo, vel Pœnitentiæ sacramento. Gratiæ enim finis est adeptio gloriæ. Idcirco gratiam Dei in vacuum recipit, qui per eam bene vivendo æternam beatitudinem non acquirit. Melius est enim viam justitiæ ignorasse, quam post agnitionem reverti retrorsum. Simili modo, melius quodammodo est gratiam non recepisse, quam receptam perdidisse.
paras.en: Now that the mysteries of the New Testament have been commended, all are invited to perfection, the Apostle saying: [[6:1|And we helping|Adjuvantes autem]] your weakness by word, by work and by prayer; or, *helping*, that is, working together with Christ in your conversion; [[6:1|do exhort you|exhortamur]] [[6:1|that you receive not|recipiatis]] [[6:1|the grace of God|gratiam Dei]], the habitual grace that makes us pleasing to God [*gratia gratum faciens*, that is, sanctifying grace], in Baptism or in the sacrament of Penance, [[6:1|in vain|ne in vacuum]], that is, without fruit and perseverance. For the end of grace is the attainment of glory. Therefore he receives the grace of God in vain who does not, by living well through it, acquire eternal beatitude. For [[2 Pet 2:21|it had been better for them not to have known the way of justice than, after they have known it, to turn back|Melius est enim viam justitiæ ignorasse, quam post agnitionem reverti retrorsum]]. In like manner, it is in a certain way better not to have received grace than to have lost it once received.

paras.t: Quod autem Deus paratus sit gratiam dare, probatur. Ait enim Dominus per Isaiam: Tempore accepto, id est tempore opportuno et congruo, maxime novæ legis et gratiæ, exaudivi te, instanter orantem pro quocumque negotio tibi salubri. Omnis enim qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur. Et in die salutis, id est tempore liberationis humanæ factæ per Christum, adjuvi te, dando tibi supernaturale auxilium gratiæ atque virtutum: sicut ait Psalmista, Auxilium meum a Domino; et, Nisi quia Dominus adjuvit me, paulo minus habitasset in inferno anima mea. Denique præallegatam Isaiæ auctoritatem quasi exponit, applicans eam ad tempus Christi. Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, id est gratum et aptum ad gratiam promerendam, quia nunc maxime operatur meritum passionis dominicæ, ecce nunc dies salutis, id est tempus salvationis a Christo exhibitæ. Unde legitur in Actibus: Omnes Prophetæ a Samuel et deinceps annuntiaverunt dies istos.
paras.en: That God is ready to give grace is proved. [[6:2|For he saith|Ait enim]], the Lord through Isaias[[Is 49:8||]]: [[6:2|In an accepted time|Tempore accepto]], that is, in the opportune and fitting time, above all that of the new law and of grace, [[6:2|have I heard thee|exaudivi te]] when thou prayest earnestly for any matter wholesome for thee. For [[Matt 7:8|every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shall be opened|Omnis enim qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur]]. [[6:2|And in the day of salvation|Et in die salutis]], that is, in the time of man's deliverance wrought through Christ, [[6:2|have I helped thee|adjuvi te]], by giving thee the supernatural help of grace and of the virtues: as the Psalmist says, [[Ps 120:2|My help is from the Lord|Auxilium meum a Domino]]; and, [[Ps 93:17|Unless the Lord had been my helper, my soul had almost dwelt in hell.|Nisi quia Dominus adjuvit me, paulo minus habitasset in inferno anima mea]] Lastly he as it were expounds the text of Isaias cited above, applying it to the time of Christ: [[6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile]], that is, pleasing and apt for meriting grace, because now above all the merit of the Lord's passion is at work; [[6:2|behold, now is the day of salvation|ecce nunc dies salutis]], that is, the time of the salvation offered by Christ. Hence we read in the Acts: [[Acts 3:24|all the prophets, from Samuel and afterwards|Omnes Prophetæ a Samuel et deinceps]] [[Acts 3:24|have told of these days|annuntiaverunt dies istos]].

paras.t: Nemini dantes ullam offensionem, id est aliquod scandalum verbo aut facto nostro minus recto. Unde alio loco dictum est: Hoc judicate, ne ponatis fratribus offendiculum. Hoc enim est caritatis. Ut non vituperetur ministerium nostrum, id est obsequium quo Christo servimus docendo et operando. Si autem reprehensibiliter egerimus, servitium nostrum vituperatur a subditis; et scandalizantur, minusque diligenter advertunt ac implent quod eis proponitur.
paras.en: [[6:3|Giving no offence to any man|Nemini dantes ullam offensionem]], that is, any scandal by a word or deed of ours that is less than right. Hence it is said in another place: [[Rom 14:13|judge this rather, that you put not a stumblingblock|Hoc judicate, ne ponatis fratribus offendiculum]] before your brethren. For this belongs to charity. [[6:3|That our ministry be not blamed|Ut non vituperetur ministerium nostrum]], that is, the service by which we serve Christ in teaching and in working. For if we act blameworthily, our service is blamed by those under us; and they are scandalized, and less diligently heed and fulfil what is set before them.

paras.t: Sed in omnibus observantiis mandatorum atque consiliorum, exhibeamus nosmetipsos sicut Dei ministros, id est, prout decet veros famulos Christi: et primo, in multa patientia, id est copiosa et prompta tolerantia adversitatum, ne passio tristitiæ regnet in nobis: in patientia, inquam, servanda in tribulationibus, id est afflictionibus a quocumque inflictis, in necessitatibus, id est penuriis victus atque vestitus, in angustiis, id est cordis pressuris; in plagis, in carceribus, quibus læsi captiique fuimus, ne liberi et incolumes prædicemus ubique; in seditionibus contra nos motis, in laboribus manualibus pro alimonia corporis, in vigiliis propter protractionem prædicationis et orationis, in jejuniis pro carne domanda et gratia impetranda, in castitate mentis et corporis, in scientia, id est notitia eorum quæ ad salutem exiguntur, in longanimitate, id est longa et certa exspectatione futuræ beatitudinis, in suavitate, id est mentis dulcedine, et blanda quadam applicatione ad proximum, in Spiritu Sancto, id est in omni directione Spiritus Sancti: in veritate non ficta, id est non simulata aut falsa, qualem habent hypocritæ: unde dicit Joannes, Non diligamus verbo, neque lingua, sed opere et veritate; in verbo veritatis, id est prædicatione Christi, qui est via, veritas et vita, seu evangelicæ theoriæ, in virtute Dei, id est divinæ potestati semper innitendo, non propriis viribus; per arma justitiæ, id est virtutes seu opera virtuosa, animam munientia per modum armorum, a dextris, id est in prosperis, a sinistris, id est adversis, quatenus nec in prosperis erigamur, nec adversis dejiciamur, sed animo roborato in gratia, regia semper via tendamus ad patriam electorum.
paras.en: [[6:4|But in all things|Sed in omnibus]], in all the observances of the commandments and of the counsels, [[6:4|let us exhibit ourselves as the ministers of God|exhibeamus nosmetipsos sicut Dei ministros]], that is, as befits true servants of Christ: and first, [[6:4|in much patience|in multa patientia]], that is, in abundant and ready endurance of adversities, lest the passion of sadness reign in us; in patience, I say, to be kept [[6:4|in tribulation|in tribulationibus]], that is, in afflictions inflicted by anyone, [[6:4|in necessities|in necessitatibus]], that is, in want of food and clothing, [[6:4|in distresses|in angustiis]], that is, in oppressions of the heart; [[6:5|in stripes, in prisons|in plagis, in carceribus]], by which we have been hurt and held captive, so that we should not preach everywhere free and unharmed; [[6:5|in seditions|in seditionibus]] stirred up against us, [[6:5|in labours|in laboribus]] of the hands for the nourishment of the body, [[6:5|in watchings|in vigiliis]] because preaching and prayer are drawn out at length, [[6:5|in fastings|in jejuniis]] to tame the flesh and to obtain grace, [[6:6|in chastity|in castitate]] of mind and body, [[6:6|in knowledge|in scientia]], that is, acquaintance with the things required for salvation, [[6:6|in longsuffering|in longanimitate]], that is, long and sure expectation of the beatitude to come, [[6:6|in sweetness|in suavitate]], that is, sweetness of mind and a certain gentle bearing toward our neighbour, [[6:6|in the Holy Ghost|in Spiritu Sancto]], that is, under every guidance of the Holy Ghost; [[6:6|in charity unfeigned|in veritate non ficta]] [the text here reads *in veritate*, “in truth”; the Apostle has *in caritate*, “in charity”, which suits Denis’s gloss and his quotation of John on love], that is, not feigned or false, such as hypocrites have: hence John says, [[1 John 3:18|let us not love in word nor in tongue, but in deed and in truth|Non diligamus verbo, neque lingua, sed opere et veritate]]; [[6:7|in the word of truth|in verbo veritatis]], that is, in the preaching of Christ, who is [[John 14:6|the way, and the truth, and the life|via, veritas et vita]], or of the doctrine of the Gospel, [[6:7|in the power of God|in virtute Dei]], that is, ever leaning on the divine power, not on our own strength; [[6:7|by the armour of justice|per arma justitiæ]], that is, the virtues or virtuous works, which guard the soul after the manner of armour, [[6:7|on the right hand|a dextris]], that is, in prosperity, [[6:7|and on the left|a sinistris]], that is, in adversity: so that we be neither lifted up in prosperity nor cast down in adversity, but with a soul strengthened in grace may ever make our way by the royal road to the fatherland of the elect.

paras.t: Exhibeamus insuper nos Dei ministros per gloriam et ignobilitatem, id est honorationem et vilipensionem, ut sive glorificemur ab hominibus, sive vilipendamur ab eis, in Christi servitio firmiter stemus; per infamiam quoque et bonam famam, id est, sive diffamemur, sive celebre nomen habeamus coram hominibus, in Christo stabiliter perseveremus, non curantes laudes aut vituperia hominum. Ut seductores reputati a multis errantibus, et veraces sumus verbo ac rebus, sicut qui ignoti, quasi a Deo reprobati secundum opinionem illorum, et tamen cogniti sumus Deo per approbationem.
paras.en: Let us moreover exhibit ourselves as ministers of God [[6:8|by honour and dishonour|per gloriam et ignobilitatem]], that is, through being honoured and being despised: so that, whether we are glorified by men or despised by them, we may stand firm in the service of Christ; [[6:8|by evil report|per infamiam]] also [[6:8|and good report|et bonam famam]], that is, whether we are defamed or have a famous name before men, let us persevere steadfastly in Christ, caring nothing for the praises or reproaches of men. [[6:8|As deceivers|Ut seductores]], so reckoned by many who are in error, [[6:8|and yet true|et veraces]] we are, in word and in deed; [[6:8|as unknown|sicut qui ignoti]], as though rejected by God in their opinion, [[6:8|and yet known|et tamen cogniti]] we are to God, by His approval.

paras.t: Quasi morientes vitam naturalem perdendo: quotidie enim putabant quidam adversarii fidei Apostolos occidendos; et ecce vivimus, Deo nos conservante in vita naturæ et gratiæ. Ut castigati, id est Deo permittente flagellati pro culpis nostris vel aliorum, vel propter exemplum atque coronam (Deus enim flagellat omnem filium quem recipit, ut Salomon loquitur), et non mortificati, id est non occisi: sæpe enim a morte corporali divina virtute erepti sunt. Unde fertur in Psalmo: Castigans castigavit me Dominus, et morti non tradidit me.
paras.en: [[6:9|As dying|Quasi morientes]], as losing our natural life: for every day certain adversaries of the faith thought that the Apostles should be killed; [[6:9|and behold we live|et ecce vivimus]], God preserving us in the life of nature and of grace; [[6:9|as chastised|Ut castigati]], that is, scourged by God’s permission for our own faults or those of others, or for an example and a crown (for God [[Heb 12:6|scourgeth every son whom he receiveth|flagellat omnem filium quem recipit]], as Solomon says[[Prov 3:12||]] [the margin gives Prov. iii, 11 and Hebr. xii, 6; the words are those of Hebrews 12:6, where the Apostle quotes Proverbs 3:11–12]), [[6:9|and not killed|et non mortificati]], that is, not slain: for they were often snatched from bodily death by the divine power. Hence it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 117:18|The Lord chastising hath chastised me: but he hath not delivered me over to death.|Castigans castigavit me Dominus, et morti non tradidit me]]

paras.t: Quasi tristes propter adversa, semper autem gaudentes in Domino, per veram patientiam et consolationem internam. Propter quod in Actibus recolitur: Ibant Apostoli gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati. Sicut egentes temporalibus bonis, secundum veritatem, vel spiritualibus donis, secundum errantium suspiciones, multos autem, id est omnes quos ad Christum convertimus, sumus locupletantes spiritualibus bonis. Tanquam nihil habentes, quoniam omnia dereliquimus propter Christum, et omnia possidentes, quantum ad necessitatem vel utilitatem: timentibus quippe Deum nihil deest. Unde dicit Salvator: Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis. Christus quoque subjecit Apostolis animata et inanimata, dæmones, et homines, quorum peccata solvere et non solvere potuerunt.
paras.en: [[6:10|As sorrowful|Quasi tristes]] on account of adversities, [[6:10|yet always rejoicing|semper autem gaudentes]] in the Lord, through true patience and inward consolation. For this reason it is recalled in the Acts that the Apostles [[Acts 5:41|went from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus|Ibant Apostoli gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati]]. [[6:10|As needy|Sicut egentes]] of temporal goods, in truth, or of spiritual gifts, in the suspicions of those who err, [[6:10|yet enriching|locupletantes]] with spiritual goods [[6:10|many|multos autem]], that is, all whom we convert to Christ. [[6:10|As having nothing|Tanquam nihil habentes]], since we have forsaken all things for Christ, [[6:10|and possessing all things|et omnia possidentes]], as far as need or usefulness goes: for nothing is lacking to those who fear God[[Ps 33:10||]]. Hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|Primum quærite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis]]. Christ also made subject to the Apostles things animate and inanimate, devils[[Matt 10:8||]][[Luke 10:17||]][[Luke 10:19||]], and men, whose sins they could loose and not loose[[Matt 18:18||]].

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit se ista loqui ex caritatis fervore. Os nostrum patet ad vos, id est, ad vestram informationem apertum est, o Corinthii, quoniam de ministerii mei dignitate, Evangelii veritate, propriæ quoque personæ commendatione, jam multa locutus sum vobis. Cor nostrum dilatatum est spiritualiter latitudine caritatis, id est, affectus noster interior extendit mentem nostram ad vos.
paras.en: Next he shows that he says these things out of the fervour of charity. [[6:11|Our mouth is open to you|Os nostrum patet ad vos]], that is, it is opened for your instruction, [[6:11|O ye Corinthians|o Corinthii]], for I have now said much to you about the dignity of my ministry, the truth of the Gospel, and also in commendation of my own person; [[6:11|our heart is enlarged|Cor nostrum dilatatum est]] spiritually with the breadth of charity, that is, our inward affection stretches out our mind toward you.

paras.t: Non angustiamini in nobis, id est, ex parte nostri nolite angustias seu minorationes scientiæ atque virtutum incurrere: nos enim parati sumus omnia nostra vobis communicare, et cor vestrum dilatare ad diligendum cœlestia. Angustiamini autem, id est, confringimini ac minoramini, in cordibus vestris duris, quæ ob suam malitiam non dilatantur per copiosam spiritualium receptionem bonorum: hoc est, parvitatem et paupertatem vestræ scientiæ atque virtutis nolite adscribere nobis, sed propriis cordibus incapacibus et indignis […]
paras.en: [[6:12|You are not straitened in us|Non angustiamini in nobis]], that is, do not on our account incur straitness or lessening of knowledge and of virtue: for we are ready to share all that is ours with you, and to enlarge your heart to love heavenly things. But [[6:12|you are straitened|Angustiamini]], that is, you are crushed and made less, [[6:12|in your own bowels|in cordibus vestris]] [Denis reads *cordibus*, “hearts”, where the Vulgate has *visceribus*, “bowels”], your hard hearts, which because of their malice are not enlarged by a plentiful reception of spiritual goods: that is, do not ascribe to us the smallness and poverty of your knowledge and virtue, but to your own hearts, incapable and unworthy […]

paras.t: […]mus, videlicet visionem Dei per speciem, quæ est tota merces, tanquam filiis meis spiritualibus dico: Dilatamini et vos corde, quemadmodum dilatatum est cor nostrum.
paras.en: […], namely the vision of God by sight [*per speciem*: seeing Him as He is, no longer by faith], which is the whole reward. [[6:13|I speak|dico]] [[6:13|as to my children|tanquam filiis]], my spiritual children: [[6:13|be you also enlarged|Dilatamini et vos]] in heart, just as our heart is enlarged.

paras.t: Nolite jugum ducere, id est societatem aut familiaritatem habere, cum infidelibus et perversis. Jugum enim a jungendo nomen sortitur. Sicut ergo dilectio est jugum Christi, per quod ei nectuntur, et ab eo ducuntur electi, sic jugum diaboli est peccatum. Idcirco iniquis et perfidis jungi non debemus, id est communicare eorum peccatis, imo et occasiones hujus communionis vitare oportet, videlicet societatem et familiaritatem. Hujus ratio subditur: Quæ enim participatio, id est mutua communio seu convenientia, justitiæ cum iniquitate? Nulla utique, quum sint omnino contrariæ. Vos autem justi estis per fidem formatam, illi vero iniqui: non ergo jungi debetis. Aut quæ societas luci ad tenebras? Nulla, videlicet naturalis ac fixa; sed lux tenebras pellit. Vos autem per Dei cognitionem lux estis, illi vero tenebris ignorantiæ pleni.
paras.en: [[6:14|Bear not the yoke|Nolite jugum ducere]], that is, have no fellowship or familiarity, [[6:14|with unbelievers|cum infidelibus]] and the perverse. For the yoke takes its name from joining [*jugum*, “yoke”, from *jungere*, “to join”]. As then love is the yoke of Christ, by which the elect are bound to Him and led by Him, so the yoke of the devil is sin. Therefore we ought not to be joined to the wicked and faithless, that is, to share in their sins; nay, we must also avoid the occasions of this communion, namely fellowship and familiarity. The reason for this follows: [[6:14|For what participation|Quæ enim participatio]], that is, mutual communion or agreement, [[6:14|hath justice with injustice|justitiæ cum iniquitate]]? None at all, since they are wholly contrary. Now you are just through formed faith [that is, faith given its form by charity], but they are wicked: therefore you ought not to be joined. [[6:14|Or what fellowship hath light with darkness|Aut quæ societas luci ad tenebras]]? None, that is, none natural and settled; rather, light drives out darkness. Now you are light through the knowledge of God, but they are full of the darkness of ignorance.

paras.t: Quæ autem conventio Christi ad Belial? Nulla plane. Belial autem interpretatur apostata, quo significatur diabolus; sed his duobus dominis nemo potest servire. Vos igitur Christiani, cum filiis Belial nolite conjungi. Aut quæ pars, id est communio, fideli cum infideli?
paras.en: [[6:15|And what concord hath Christ with Belial|Quæ autem conventio Christi ad Belial]]? None whatever. Now *Belial* is interpreted “apostate”, by which the devil is signified; but [[Matt 6:24|no man can serve two masters|duobus dominis nemo potest servire]] such as these. You Christians, therefore, do not join yourselves with the sons of Belial. [[6:15|Or what part|Aut quæ pars]], that is, communion, [[6:15|hath the faithful with the unbeliever|fideli cum infideli]]?

paras.t: Quis autem consensus templo Dei, id est personæ fidelis, in qua per gratiam habitat Deus, cum idolis? id est idololatris, qui idola sunt per similitudinem, juxta illud in Psalmo, Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea. Non ergo debetis illis sociari.
paras.en: [[6:16|And what agreement hath the temple of God|Quis autem consensus templo Dei]], that is, the faithful person in whom God dwells by grace[[1 Cor 3:16||]], [[6:16|with idols|cum idolis]]? that is, with idolaters, who are idols by likeness, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 134:18|let them that make them be like to them|Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxiv, 18; the words are those of Ps 134:18, and of Ps 113:16]. You ought not then to be associated with them.

paras.t: Vos enim, in quorum cordibus habitat Deus, estis templum animatum ac mysticum Dei vivi, sicut dicit Dominus per Moysen, Ezechielem, atque Joannem in Apocalypsi: Quoniam inhabitabo in illis, id est, intima mentis electorum inhabitabo per caritatem et gratiam, et inambulabo, id est, in corde eorum quasi in paradiso voluptatis conversabor, quia deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum. Inambulabo autem, id est, eos faciam ambulare de virtute in virtutem, et de via ad patriam; et ero illorum Deus, non solum generaliter, sicut omnium Deus sum propter universalem creationem ac providentiam, sed singulariter valde, dirigendo, protegendo, finaliterque salvando; et ipsi erunt mihi, id est ad honorem et gloriam nominis mei, populus, colendo et diligendo me super omnia: sicut in prima sua epistola asserit Petrus, Vos genus electum, gens sancta, populus acquisitionis; et Psalmista, Beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo.
paras.en: [[6:16|For you|Vos enim]], in whose hearts God dwells, [[6:16|are the temple|estis templum]], living and mystical, [[6:16|of the living God|Dei vivi]], [[6:16|as God saith|sicut dicit Dominus]] through Moses[[Ex 29:45||]][[Lev 26:11||]], Ezechiel[[Ezech 37:27||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xlvi, 9, which does not fit; the words are in Ezech 37:27] and John in the Apocalypse[[Apoc 21:3||]]: [[6:16|I will dwell in them|Quoniam inhabitabo in illis]], that is, I will dwell in the inmost mind of the elect by charity and grace, [[6:16|and walk|et inambulabo]], that is, I will go about in their heart as in a paradise of pleasure, because [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum]]. [[6:16|walk|Inambulabo]], moreover, means: I will make them walk [[Ps 83:8|from virtue to virtue|de virtute in virtutem]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxviii, 8; the words are those of Ps 83:8], and from the way to the fatherland; [[6:16|and I will be their God|et ero illorum Deus]], not only in general, as I am the God of all by universal creation and providence, but in a very special way, by directing, protecting, and at the last saving them; [[6:16|and they shall be|et ipsi erunt mihi]], that is, for the honour and glory of my name, [[6:16|my people|populus]], worshipping and loving me above all things: as Peter asserts in his first epistle, [[1 Pet 2:9|you are a chosen generation|Vos genus electum]], [[1 Pet 2:9|a holy nation, a purchased people|gens sancta, populus acquisitionis]]; and the Psalmist, [[Ps 149:4|the Lord is well pleased with his people|Beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo]].

paras.t: Ex dictis infert Apostolus admonitionem intentam. Propter quod, id est, quia non est societas inter prædicta, exite spiritualiter, et si fieri potest et expedit, etiam corporaliter, de medio eorum, id est de conventu pravorum. Quid enim paleis ad triticum? Hoc est, nolite cordis similitudine eis conjungi, sed fugite actus eorum. Et separamini ab eis, loco vel corde, dicit Dominus; et immundum ne tetigeritis, id est, peccato nolite consentire. Digni enim sunt morte, non solum qui faciunt, sed etiam qui consenserint.
paras.en: From what has been said the Apostle draws the admonition he intends. [[6:17|Wherefore|Propter quod]], that is, because there is no fellowship between the things just named, [[6:17|go out|exite]] spiritually, and, if it can be done and is expedient, bodily too, [[6:17|from among them|de medio eorum]], that is, from the company of the wicked. For [[Jer 23:28|what hath the chaff to do with the wheat|Quid enim paleis ad triticum]]? [the margin gives Jer. xxxiii, 28; the words are those of Jer 23:28] That is, do not be joined to them by likeness of heart, but flee their deeds; [[6:17|and be ye separate|Et separamini]] from them, in place or in heart, [[6:17|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]; [[6:17|and touch not the unclean thing|et immundum ne tetigeritis]], that is, do not consent to sin. For they [[Rom 1:32|are worthy of death|Digni enim sunt morte]], [[Rom 1:32|and not only they that do them|non solum qui faciunt]], [[Rom 1:32|but they also that consent|sed etiam qui consenserint]].

paras.t: Et ego recipiam vos, id est, pie amplectar venientes ad me brachiis pietatis: de quibus per Prophetam loquor, Portavi vos in brachiis meis. Et ero vobis in patrem, id est, paterne vos fovebo ac diligam, et vos eritis mihi in filios, quantum ad viros, et filias, quantum ad feminas, dicit Dominus Deus omnipotens.
paras.en: [[6:18|And I will receive you|Et ego recipiam vos]], that is, I will lovingly embrace those who come to me, with the arms of loving-kindness, of which I speak through the Prophet: [[Osee 11:3|I carried them in my arms|Portavi vos in brachiis meis]] [Denis has *vos*, “you”, where the prophet has “them”]. [[6:18|And will be a Father to you|Et ero vobis in patrem]], that is, I will cherish and love you as a father, [[6:18|and you shall be my sons|et vos eritis mihi in filios]], as regards men, [[6:18|and daughters|et filias]], as regards women, [[6:18|saith the Lord Almighty|dicit Dominus Deus omnipotens]].

paras.t: Porro Scriptura hic allegata, quantum ad sensum in diversis sacræ paginæ locis habetur. Pro eo enim quod hic dictum est, Inhabitabo in illis, scriptum est in Levitico: Ponam tabernaculum meum in medio vestri. Pro eo quod subditur, Et inambulabo, legitur in Deuteronomio: Dominus Deus tuus ambulat in medio castrorum. Totum tamen istud, et item quod subditur, Et ero illorum Deus, et ipsi erunt mihi populus, etc., in Levitico includitur. Ei quoque quod subinfertur, Exite de medio eorum, consonat quod Petrus disseruit: Separamini, inquiens, a generatione hac prava. Sed et in Apocalypsi ait Scriptura: Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis: et ipsi populus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit illorum Deus. Quæ utique verba plena sunt omni dulcedine, caritate atque fiducia.
paras.en: Now the Scripture cited here is found, as to its sense, in various places of the sacred page. For in place of what is said here, [[6:16|I will dwell in them|Inhabitabo in illis]], it is written in Leviticus: [[Lev 26:11|I will set my tabernacle in the midst of you|Ponam tabernaculum meum in medio vestri]]. In place of what follows, [[6:16|and walk|Et inambulabo]], we read in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 23:14|the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp|Dominus Deus tuus ambulat in medio castrorum]]. Yet the whole of this, and likewise what follows, [[6:16|And I will be their God|Et ero illorum Deus]], [[6:16|and they shall be my people|et ipsi erunt mihi populus]], etc., is contained in Leviticus[[Lev 26:12||]]. With what is added next, [[6:17|Go out from among them|Exite de medio eorum]], agrees what Peter declared: Be ye separate, he said, [[Acts 2:40|from this perverse generation|a generatione hac prava]] [Denis reads *Separamini*, “be ye separate”, where the Vulgate has *Salvamini*, “save yourselves”]. And in the Apocalypse too the Scripture says: [[Apoc 21:3|Behold the tabernacle of God with men: and he will dwell with them. And they shall be his people: and God himself with them shall be their God|Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis: et ipsi populus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit illorum Deus]]. These words are surely full of all sweetness, charity and confidence.

7.title: Expositio capituli septimi: Has igitur habentes promissiones
7.title_en: Exposition of the seventh chapter: Having therefore these promises

paras.t: Ex præinductis in fine præcedentis capituli infert Apostolus admonitionem salubrem, et ait : Has igitur habentes promissiones, o carissimi fratres, immediate expressas, videlicet quod Deus habitabit et ambulabit in nobis, recipietque nos, et erit in nobis, mundemus nos per veram confessionem (omnia enim in confessione lavantur), per contritionem, per dominicæ passionis memoriam, præsertim per divini amoris accensionem, quoniam caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum, ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, id est ab universis peccatis carnalibus, ut sunt gula, luxuria, et spiritualibus, ut sunt invidia, superbia ; perficientes sanctificationem, id est, inchoatam in Baptismo vel Pœnitentia sanctitatem ad perfectionem ducentes, perseverando ac proficiendo in bonis usque in finem : et hoc, in timore Dei casto ac filiali : de quo in Ecclesiastico dicitur, Qui sine timore est, justificari non potest ; atque in Psalmo, Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus.
paras.en: From what was set down at the end of the preceding chapter the Apostle draws a wholesome admonition, and says: [[7:1|Having therefore these promises|Has igitur habentes promissiones]], [[7:1|dearly beloved|o carissimi]] brethren, the promises set out just before, namely that God will dwell and walk in us, and will receive us, and will be in us, [[7:1|let us cleanse ourselves|mundemus nos]] by true confession[[Ps 31:5||]][[Prov 28:13||]] [the margin gives Prov. xxxiii, 13; Proverbs has no thirty-third chapter, and the verse meant is Prov 28:13] (for all things are washed away in confession), by contrition, by remembrance of the Lord's passion, and above all by the kindling of divine love, since [[1 Pet 4:8|charity covereth a multitude of sins|caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum]]; [[7:1|from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit|ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus]], that is, from all sins of the flesh, such as gluttony and lust, and of the spirit, such as envy and pride; [[7:1|perfecting sanctification|perficientes sanctificationem]], that is, bringing to perfection the holiness begun in Baptism or in Penance, by persevering and advancing in good things to the end: and this [[7:1|in the fear of God|in timore Dei]], a chaste and filial fear, of which it is said in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 1:28|he that is without fear, cannot be justified|Qui sine timore est, justificari non potest]]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 33:10|Fear the Lord, all ye his saints|Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxii, 10; the verse is Ps 33:10].

paras.t: Capite nos, id est, verba nostra sapienter pensate, et nos ipsos in exemplum accipite. Neminem læsimus post nostram conversionem, id est, nullum ad peccatum induximus directe, verbo vel opere, neminem corrupimus per falsam doctrinam, neminem circumvenimus, id est, defraudando decepimus. Non ad condemnationem vestram dico, id est, non ideo ista commemoro, ut aggravem vestra peccata, vosque relinquam ac pereatis. Prædiximus enim, et supra jam scripsimus, quod in cordibus nostris estis scripti per curam et caritatis affectum, et jugem memoriam, ad commoriendum et convivendum : id est, in tantum vos meo cordi impressi, ut pro vestra salute paratus sim mori, aut manere in vita præsenti, ut instruam vos.
paras.en: [[7:2|Receive us|Capite nos]] [*capite*, literally "take in" or "grasp"], that is, weigh our words wisely, and take us ourselves as an example. [[7:2|We have injured no man|Neminem læsimus]] since our conversion, that is, we have led no one into sin directly, by word or deed; [[7:2|we have corrupted no man|neminem corrupimus]] by false teaching; [[7:2|we have overreached no man|neminem circumvenimus]], that is, we have deceived no one by defrauding him. [[7:3|I speak not this to your condemnation|Non ad condemnationem vestram dico]], that is, I do not recall these things in order to make your sins heavier, and to abandon you so that you perish. [[7:3|For we have said before|Prædiximus enim]], and have already written above, [[7:3|that you are in our hearts|quod in cordibus nostris estis]], written there[[2 Cor 3:2||]] by care and the affection of charity and constant remembrance, [[7:3|to die together and to live together|ad commoriendum et convivendum]]: that is, I have so impressed you on my heart that for your salvation I am ready to die, or to remain in the present life to instruct you.

paras.t: Multa mihi fiducia est apud vos, id est, de vestra caritate et pietate multum confido, et firmiter spero de felicitate vestra futura ; multa mihi gloriatio inest spiritualis in Domino, pro vobis, id est ex consideratione gratiæ vobis concessæ : repletus sum consolatione, audita vestra emendatione, superabundo gaudio spirituali, propter beneficia Dei vobis collata, in omni tribulatione nostra, quam ab adversariis fidei patimur. Nam et quum venissemus in Macedoniam, nullam requiem habuit caro nostra, id est nos ipsi. Ponit enim partem pro toto : nam superius dixit, Non habui requiem spiritui meo. Sed omnem, id est multiplicem seu perfectam, tribulationem, videlicet exteriorem et interiorem. foris pugnæ, id est impugnationes a perversis ac perfidis, intus, id est in corde, fuerunt timores paternæ sollicitudinis pro Ecclesiis Dei ne subverterentur. Sed qui consolatur humiles, consolatus est nos Deus in adventu Titi : de cujus adventu gavisi sumus, propter adjutorium quod nobis impendit.
paras.en: [[7:4|Great is my confidence for you|Multa mihi fiducia est apud vos]], that is, I have great confidence in your charity and piety, and firmly hope for your future happiness; [[7:4|great is my glorying|multa mihi gloriatio]], a spiritual glorying in the Lord, [[7:4|for you|pro vobis]], that is, from considering the grace granted to you: [[7:4|I am filled with comfort|repletus sum consolatione]], having heard of your amendment; [[7:4|I exceedingly abound with joy|superabundo gaudio]], spiritual joy, because of the benefits of God bestowed on you, [[7:4|in all our tribulation|in omni tribulatione nostra]], which we suffer from the adversaries of the faith. [[7:5|For also, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest|Nam et quum venissemus in Macedoniam, nullam requiem habuit caro nostra]], that is, we ourselves. For he puts the part for the whole: for above he said, [[2 Cor 2:13|I had no rest in my spirit|Non habui requiem spiritui meo]]. [[7:5|but|Sed]] [[7:5|all|omnem]], that is, manifold or complete, [[7:5|tribulation|tribulationem]], namely outward and inward: [[7:5|Combats without|foris pugnæ]], that is, assaults from the perverse and the faithless; [[7:5|within|intus]], that is, in the heart, there were [[7:5|fears|timores]] of fatherly anxiety for the Churches of God, lest they be overthrown. [[7:6|But God, who comforteth the humble, comforted us by the coming of Titus|Sed qui consolatur humiles, consolatus est nos Deus in adventu Titi]]: at whose coming we rejoiced, because of the help he gave us.

paras.t: Non solum autem in adventu ejus consolatus est nos Deus, sed etiam a Deo principaliter consolati sumus, in consolatione, id est per consolationem, qua consolatus est nos Titus Dei minister in vobis, id est de vestra correctione, referens nobis vestrum desiderium pro gratia acquirenda, vel pro mea præsentia, vestrum fletum propter peccata præterita, vestram æmulationem, id est bonum zelum, pro me, id est pro nostra defensione contra detractores nostros et pseudoapostolos, quibus rationabiliter indignati estis ; ita ut magis gauderem de vestra prosperitate, quam dolui de mea adversitate.
paras.en: [[7:7|And not by his coming only|Non solum autem in adventu ejus]] did God comfort us, [[7:7|but also|sed etiam]] we were comforted, chiefly by God, [[7:7|by the consolation|in consolatione]], that is, through the consolation [[7:7|wherewith|qua]] Titus, the minister of God, [[7:7|comforted|consolatus est]] us [Denis takes *consolatus est* as active, "comforted", where the Douay-Rheims has "was comforted"] [[7:7|in you|in vobis]], that is, over your correction, [[7:7|relating to us your desire|referens nobis vestrum desiderium]] to obtain grace, or for my presence, [[7:7|your mourning|vestrum fletum]] for your past sins, [[7:7|your zeal|vestram æmulationem]], that is, a good zeal, [[7:7|for me|pro me]], that is, in our defence against our detractors and the false apostles, with whom you were rightly indignant; [[7:7|so that I rejoiced the more|ita ut magis gauderem]] at your prosperity than I grieved at my adversity.

paras.t: Denique, quod consolatus sim, patet : Quoniam etsi contristavi vos in epistola superiori, in qua dure correpti estis, non me pœnitet hoc fecisse. Etsi, id est Licet, pœnitere me vos contristasse, considerando tristitiam sub ratione tristitiæ tantum, secundum quem modum non habet rationem boni et appetibilis ; tamen videns quod epistola illa, etsi ad horam, vos contristavit, nunc gaudeo de vestra contristatione pœnitentiali ; non quia contristati estis in genere, seu qualitercumque (non enim omnis tristitia bona est), sed quia contristati estis ad pœnitentiam salutarem ac sacramentalem, id est, vestra contristatio bonum finem sortita est : nam ad pœnitentiam vos induxit, quæ est dolor de malis præteritis. Contristati estis secundum Deum, id est secundum beneplacitum Dei, dolentes de peccatis vestris : quod complacet Deo, qui ait per Ezechielem, Confundimini et erubescite super viis vestris ; et alibi, Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum ; ut in nullo, id est nec in blandis nec in prosperis, detrimentum salutis patiamini ex nobis, id est, ne nos aliquo modo simus vobis occasio detrimenti, sed totum quod pro vobis agimus, vestræ prosit saluti.
paras.en: Lastly, that I have been comforted is plain: [[7:8|For although I made you sorrowful by my epistle|Quoniam etsi contristavi vos in epistola]], the former one, in which you were sharply rebuked, [[7:8|I do not repent|non me pœnitet]] of having done it. [[7:8|And if|Etsi]], that is, granted that, I might repent of having made you sorrowful, considering sorrow purely under the aspect of sorrow, in which respect it has not the nature of something good and desirable, yet, [[7:8|seeing that the same epistle (although but for a time) did make you sorrowful|videns quod epistola illa, etsi ad horam, vos contristavit]], [[7:9|Now I am glad|nunc gaudeo]] of your penitential sorrow; [[7:9|not because you were made sorrowful|non quia contristati estis]] in general, or in any way whatever (for not all sorrow is good), [[7:9|but because you were made sorrowful unto penance|sed quia contristati estis ad pœnitentiam]], a saving and sacramental penance: that is, your sorrow has come to a good end, for it has led you to penance, which is grief for past evils. [[7:9|you were made sorrowful according to God|Contristati estis secundum Deum]], that is, according to God's good pleasure, grieving for your sins: which is pleasing to God, who says by Ezechiel, [[Ezech 36:32|be confounded, and ashamed at your own ways|Confundimini et erubescite super viis vestris]]; and elsewhere, [[Matt 4:17|Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand|Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum]] [no reference in the margin; these are Christ's words in Matt 4:17, and the Baptist's in Matt 3:2]; [[7:9|in nothing|ut in nullo]], that is, neither in soft things nor in prosperous ones, [[7:9|that you might suffer damage|detrimentum salutis patiamini]] to your salvation [[7:9|by us|ex nobis]]: that is, that we may in no way be an occasion of harm to you, but that all we do for you may profit your salvation.

paras.t: Quæ enim secundum Deum tristitia est, id est tristitia ordinata de peccato commisso, pœnitentiam, id est cessationem a malo et satisfactionem tendentem in salutem stabilem, id est veram atque perpetuam beatitudinem promerentem, operatur in genere causæ formalis. De hac bona tristitia scriptum est : Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia ; et iterum, Per tristitiam vultus corrigitur animus delinquentis. De prædicta quoque stabili salute alibi dicitur : Israel salvatus est in Domino salute æterna. Sæculi autem tristitia, id est dolor de amissione temporalium rerum et manifestatione propriæ iniquitatis, mortem culpæ operatur, id est, ad peccandum inducit : imo et mortem naturæ consciscit, quoniam nulla passio animæ adeo corruptiva atque contraria vitæ est, sicut tristitia, prout in prima secundæ Thomas pulchre demonstrat. Propter quod Salomon loquitur : Spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa. In Ecclesiastico quoque legitur : Multos occidit tristitia.
paras.en: [[7:10|For the sorrow that is according to God|Quæ enim secundum Deum tristitia est]], that is, a rightly ordered sorrow for sin committed, [[7:10|worketh|operatur]], in the order of formal cause [that is, as what makes penance what it is, not as an outside agent], [[7:10|penance|pœnitentiam]], that is, a ceasing from evil and a satisfaction, tending [[7:10|steadfast unto salvation|in salutem stabilem]], that is, meriting true and everlasting beatitude. Of this good sorrow it is written: [[Eccles 7:5|The heart of the wise is where there is mourning, and the heart of fools where there is mirth|Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia]] [the margin gives Eccle. vii, 3; the verse is Eccles 7:5. Where the Douay-Rheims has "mourning" the Latin has *tristitia*, "sorrow", the Apostle's word here]; and again, [[Eccles 7:4|by the sadness of the countenance the mind of the offender is corrected|Per tristitiam vultus corrigitur animus delinquentis]]. Of the steadfast salvation just named it is said elsewhere: [[Is 45:17|Israel is saved in the Lord with an eternal salvation|Israel salvatus est in Domino salute æterna]]. [[7:10|but the sorrow of the world|Sæculi autem tristitia]], that is, grief at the loss of temporal things and at the laying bare of one's own wickedness, [[7:10|worketh death|mortem culpæ operatur]], the death of guilt: that is, it leads to sinning; nay, it even brings on the death of nature [that is, bodily death], since no passion of the soul is so destructive and so contrary to life as sorrow, as Thomas finely shows in the First Part of the Second Part [that is, of the *Summa theologiae*, I-II, q. 37, a. 4]. Wherefore Solomon says: [[Prov 17:22|a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones|Spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa]]. In Ecclesiasticus too we read: [[Ecclus 30:25|sadness hath killed many|Multos occidit tristitia]].

paras.t: Insuper, quod tristitia ista secundum Deum operativa sit pœnitentiæ in salutem, ostendit Apostolus. Ecce enim hoc ipsum, secundum Deum contristari vos, id est tristitia hæc Domino placens, quantam in vobis operatur sollicitudinem placandi Deum et cavendi a peccatis : sed defensionem, id est, resistentiam contra tentationes diaboli et incentiva peccati : pœnitens enim munit et armat se contra causas peccandi ; sed indignationem, id est horrorem peccati, vel abominationem contra vos ipsos, qui tam prave egistis ; sed timorem divini judicii, infernalis tormenti, similisque peccati : pœnitens nempe formidat incidere manus Dei viventis, et timet ne denuo peccet ; sed desiderium veniæ ac profectus ; sed æmulationem, id est bonorum imitationem ac zelum. Unde in Apocalypsi dicitur : Æmulare ergo, et pœnitentiam age. Vel, Æmulationem, id est zelum contra falsos qui vos ad vitia induxerunt. Sed vindictam, id est punitionem peccati. Qui enim veraciter pœnitet, peccata sua in se ipso ulciscitur, infligendo sibi pœnam secundum culpæ mensuram. Nam et satisfactio est pars Pœnitentiæ, sicut contritio atque confessio. In omnibus agendis exhibuistis vos incontaminatos esse, id est inculpabiles, negotio christiano exercendo : id est, ita vos reformastis, ut in omnibus christianæ conversationis officiis incontaminati sitis, saltem a mortali peccato. Potest quoque specialiter accipi de negotio quod eis commisit Apostolus, circa punitionem ejus qui uxorem habuit sui patris : quod utique negotium Corinthii fideliter expediverunt.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle shows that this sorrow according to God works penance unto salvation. [[7:11|For behold this selfsame thing, that you were made sorrowful according to God|Ecce enim hoc ipsum, secundum Deum contristari vos]], that is, this sorrow that pleases the Lord, [[7:11|how great carefulness it worketh in you|quantam in vobis operatur sollicitudinem]] to appease God and to beware of sins: [[7:11|yea defence|sed defensionem]], that is, resistance against the temptations of the devil and the incitements of sin, for the penitent fortifies and arms himself against the causes of sinning; [[7:11|yea indignation|sed indignationem]], that is, horror of sin, or loathing of yourselves, who acted so wickedly; [[7:11|yea fear|sed timorem]] of the divine judgment, of the torment of hell, and of a like sin, for the penitent dreads to fall [[Heb 10:31|into the hands of the living God|manus Dei viventis]], and fears lest he sin again; [[7:11|yea desire|sed desiderium]] of pardon and of progress; [[7:11|yea zeal|sed æmulationem]], that is, the imitation of good men, and zeal [*æmulatio* means both emulation and zeal, hence the two readings]. Whence it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Be zealous therefore and do penance|Æmulare ergo, et pœnitentiam age]]. Or, [[7:11|zeal|Æmulationem]], that is, zeal against the false teachers who led you into vices. [[7:11|yea revenge|Sed vindictam]], that is, the punishment of sin. For he who truly repents takes vengeance on his sins in himself, inflicting on himself a penalty according to the measure of the guilt. For satisfaction too is a part of Penance, as are contrition and confession. [[7:11|In all things|In omnibus]] to be done [[7:11|you have shewed yourselves to be undefiled|exhibuistis vos incontaminatos esse]], that is, blameless, [[7:11|in the matter|negotio]] of carrying on the Christian life: that is, you have so reformed yourselves that in all the duties of Christian living you are undefiled, at least by mortal sin. It can also be taken specially of the matter which the Apostle entrusted to them, concerning the punishment of him who had his father's wife[[1 Cor 5:1||]]: a matter which the Corinthians certainly carried out faithfully.

paras.t: Igitur etsi scripsi vobis in præcedenti epistola, hoc feci, non solum propter eum qui fecit injuriam, id est propter correctionem fornicatoris qui rapuit patris sui uxorem, nec solum propter eum qui passus est injuriam, id est patrem cui ablata et rapta est uxor a proprio filio ; sed ad manifestandam sollicitudinem nostram, quam pro vobis, id est pro vestra salute, habemus coram Deo, id est, Deo spectante, nostrumque affectum effundendo coram eo pro vobis cum humili prece. Ideo consolati sumus de vestri correctione.
paras.en: [[7:12|Wherefore although I wrote to you|Igitur etsi scripsi vobis]] in the preceding epistle, I did it not only [[7:12|for his sake that did the wrong|propter eum qui fecit injuriam]], that is, for the correction of the fornicator who carried off his father's wife, [[7:12|nor|nec]] only [[7:12|for him that suffered it|propter eum qui passus est injuriam]], that is, the father, whose wife was taken and carried off from him by his own son; [[7:12|but to manifest our carefulness|sed ad manifestandam sollicitudinem nostram]] [[7:12|that we have for you|quam pro vobis]], that is, for your salvation, [[7:13|Before God|coram Deo]], that is, in God's sight, pouring out our affection before him for you in humble prayer. [[7:13|therefore we were comforted|Ideo consolati sumus]] at your correction.

paras.t: In consolatione autem nostra jam sæpe prædicta, id est ultra hanc consolationem, abundantius magis, id est abundantissime, vel plus quam ante doluimus, gavisi sumus super, id est de, gaudio Titi, ita ut gaudium ejus esset objectum atque materia gaudii nostri, quia refectus est, id est recreatus et confortatus, spiritus ejus paulo ante propter vestra peccata mæstus, ab omnibus vobis de correctione, vel profectu, vel bono proposito cujuslibet vestrum. Qui enim nondum correcti sunt, se emendare decreverunt, et ita spes bona lætificat Titum.
paras.en: [[7:13|But in our consolation|In consolatione autem nostra]], so often spoken of already, that is, over and above this consolation, [[7:13|we did the more abundantly|abundantius magis]], that is, most abundantly, or more than we had grieved before, [[7:13|rejoice|gavisi sumus]] [[7:13|for|super]], that is, over, [[7:13|the joy of Titus|gaudio Titi]], so that his joy was the object and matter of our joy, [[7:13|because|quia]] [[7:13|his spirit|spiritus ejus]], a little before sorrowful because of your sins, [[7:13|was refreshed|refectus est]], that is, restored and strengthened, [[7:13|by you all|ab omnibus vobis]], through the correction, or the progress, or the good purpose of each one of you. For those who are not yet corrected have resolved to amend themselves, and so good hope gladdens Titus.

paras.t: Et si quid apud illum, id est quia de aliquo apud Titum, de vobis gloriatus sum, commendando vos, et de vestra emendatione spem bonam ei præstando, non sum confusus de hac gloriatione, quum non sim mendax inventus ; sed sicut omnia ad vestram salutem pertinentia vobis in veritate locuti sumus prædicatione vocali, vel per epistolas, ita et gloriatio nostra, quæ fuit ad Titum de vobis (ut dictum est), veritas facta est, id est ad effectum perducta ; vel, sic esse innotuit Tito, sicut ei prædixi, quoniam estis correcti et laude digni inventi.
paras.en: [[7:14|And if|Et si]] [[7:14|any thing|quid]] [[7:14|to him|apud illum]], that is, since in some matter with Titus, [[7:14|I have boasted|gloriatus sum]] [[7:14|of you|de vobis]], commending you and giving him good hope of your amendment, [[7:14|I have not been put to shame|non sum confusus]] by this boasting, since I have not been found a liar; [[7:14|but as we have spoken all things|sed sicut omnia]] that pertain to your salvation [[7:14|to you in truth|vobis in veritate locuti sumus]], by preaching aloud or by letters, [[7:14|so also our boasting that was made to Titus|ita et gloriatio nostra, quæ fuit ad Titum]] about you (as has been said), [[7:14|is found a truth|veritas facta est]] [literally "has been made truth"], that is, has been brought to effect; or, it has become known to Titus that it is so, just as I told him beforehand, since you have been found corrected and worthy of praise.

paras.t: Et viscera ejus, id est intima caritas ac desiderium Titi, abundantius nunc quam ante, quia nunc videt vestram obedientiam, in vobis sunt, id est, in vos tendunt, atque figuntur : amor enim tendit in amatum, et quiescit in ipso ; Titi, inquam, reminiscentis omnium vestrum obedientiam (retulit enim Titus Apostolo cum ingenti lætitia obedientiam Corinthiorum), quomodo cum timore cordis et tremore corporis excepistis eum cum debita reverentia, sicut et vobis præcepi tales recipere tanquam me ipsum, imo ut Christum.
paras.en: [[7:15|And his bowels|Et viscera ejus]], that is, the inmost charity and desire of Titus, [[7:15|are more abundantly|abundantius]] now than before, because he now sees your obedience, [[7:15|towards you|in vobis sunt]], that is, they tend towards you and are fixed on you: for love tends towards the beloved, and rests in it; of Titus, I say, [[7:15|remembering the obedience of you all|reminiscentis omnium vestrum obedientiam]] (for Titus related the obedience of the Corinthians to the Apostle with great gladness), [[7:15|how with fear|quomodo cum timore]] of heart [[7:15|and trembling|et tremore]] of body [[7:15|you received him|excepistis eum]] with due reverence, as I also charged you to receive such men as myself[[1 Cor 16:10||]], nay, as Christ[[Gal 4:14||]] [the margin gives Galat. v, 14; the passage meant is Gal 4:14].

paras.t: Gaudeo de hoc, et ob hoc, apud te omnibus rebus confido in vobis, sperans vos semper ad obediendum paratos, sicut et nunc obedientiam vestram expertus sum. Una equidem actio virtuosa præstat fiduciam de alia, atque majori.
paras.en: [[7:16|I rejoice|Gaudeo]] at this and because of this [the text has *apud te*, "with thee", here, which seems to be a slip] [[7:16|that in all things I have confidence in you|omnibus rebus confido in vobis]], hoping that you will always be ready to obey, as I have now found your obedience by experience. For one virtuous act gives confidence about another, and a greater one.

8.title: Declaratio capituli octavi: Notam autem facimus vobis, fratres, gratiam Dei
8.title_en: Explanation of the eighth chapter: Now we make known unto you, brethren, the grace of God

paras.t: Præterea admonet Apostolus Corinthios ad faciendam atque mittendam eleemosynam pauperibus qui erant in Jerusalem sub regimine Jacobi; proponitque Corinthiis exemplum Macedonum, dicens: Notam autem facimus vobis, fratres, gratiam Dei quæ data est in Ecclesiis Macedoniæ, id est, insinuamus vobis virtutem misericordiæ quam Deus largitus est Macedonibus (qui sunt Græci) ad fidem conversis. Ex qua virtute et gratia divinitus inspirata, moti sunt eleemosynam dare Judæis conversis in Jerusalem morantibus, qui, facta fame in Judæa, magnam habuerunt inopiam. Hoc itaque notificamus vobis, quod in multo experimento tribulationis, id est in magna tribulatione quam experti sunt, abundantia gaudii ipsorum fuit, id est, copiosa lætitia inerat eis: quia de tribulatione sua propter Christum illata, vehementer gavisi sunt, sicut dicit Salvator, Gaudete in illa hora, quia merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis; et altissima, id est spontanea multumque meritoria, paupertas eorum, puta Macedonum, abundavit, id est, abundantem effectum habuit vel ostendit, in divitias simplicitatis, id est in spiritualem opulentiam puræ intentionis et bonæ conscientiæ eorum: quia quum pauperes essent, tamen modica simplici animo tribuendo, spiritualiter ditiores effecti sunt.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle urges the Corinthians to make and send an alms for the poor who were at Jerusalem under the rule of James; and he sets before the Corinthians the example of the Macedonians, saying: [[8:1|Now we make known unto you, brethren, the grace of God that hath been given in the churches of Macedonia|Notam autem facimus vobis, fratres, gratiam Dei quæ data est in Ecclesiis Macedoniæ]], that is, we tell you of the virtue of mercy which God has bestowed on the Macedonians (who are Greeks) converted to the faith. Moved by this virtue and grace inspired by God, they gave alms to the converted Jews living at Jerusalem, who, when famine came in Judæa, were in great want. This, then, we make known to you: [[8:2|That in much experience of tribulation|quod in multo experimento tribulationis]], that is, in the great tribulation which they underwent, [[8:2|they have had abundance of joy|abundantia gaudii ipsorum fuit]], that is, plentiful gladness was in them: for they rejoiced exceedingly at the tribulation brought on them for Christ's sake, as the Saviour says: [[Luke 6:23|Be glad|Gaudete]] in that hour, for [[Matt 5:12|your reward is very great in heaven|merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]] [the margin gives both Luke 6:23 and Matt 5:12; Denis's words mix the two]; [[8:2|and their very deep|et altissima]], that is, freely chosen and highly meritorious, [[8:2|poverty|paupertas eorum]], namely that of the Macedonians, [[8:2|hath abounded|abundavit]], that is, had or showed an abundant effect, [[8:2|unto the riches of their simplicity|in divitias simplicitatis]], that is, unto the spiritual wealth of pure intention and good conscience: for though they were poor, yet by giving a little with a simple heart they were made spiritually richer.

paras.t: Quia secundum virtutem justitiæ, id est vere ac juste, testimonium illis reddo, et supra virtutem, id est ultra suam possibilitatem, voluntarii fuerunt ad dandum. Nam quum modica possiderent, multa dare optabant; tantaque dederunt, ut etiam ipsi postmodum egerent. Cum multa exhortatione obsecrantes nos gratiam et communicationem ministerii, id est, ut consentiremus ipsis in hoc, quod dare possent tantam eleemosynam, qua communicarent atque participes essent ministerii, id est obsequii pietatis, videlicet largitionis eleemosynarum, quod fit in sanctos, id est pauperes in Jerusalem commorantes: qui sancti vocantur, quoniam omnibus suis venditis, pretia ante Apostolorum pedes posuerunt, egene communiterque viventes. Quum enim Macedones pauperes essent, non videtur eis Apostolus consensisse ut darent tam multum; sed ipsi caritate fervente rogabant Apostolum ut liceret eis tanta conferre.
paras.en: [[8:3|For according to their power|Quia secundum virtutem]], that is, according to the virtue of justice [*virtus* means both "power" and "virtue"; Denis takes it here as the virtue of justice], that is, truly and justly, [[8:3|I bear them witness|testimonium illis reddo]], [[8:3|and beyond their power|et supra virtutem]], that is, beyond their means, [[8:3|they were willing|voluntarii fuerunt]] to give. For though they possessed little, they wished to give much; and they gave so much that afterwards they were themselves in want. [[8:4|With much entreaty begging of us the grace and communication of the ministry|Cum multa exhortatione obsecrantes nos gratiam et communicationem ministerii]], that is, that we would consent to their being able to give so great an alms, by which they might share and have part in the ministry, that is, in the service of piety, namely the bestowing of alms, [[8:4|that is done toward the saints|quod fit in sanctos]], that is, the poor dwelling at Jerusalem: who are called saints because, having sold all they had, they laid the prices before the feet of the Apostles[[Acts 4:34||]][[Acts 4:35||]], living poorly and in common. For since the Macedonians were poor, the Apostle seems not to have consented that they should give so much; but they, with fervent charity, begged the Apostle that they might be allowed to contribute so much.

paras.t: Et non sicut speravimus, id est, non tam moderate se habuerunt in dando sicut putavimus, sed semetipsos dederunt, id est obtulerunt, primum, id est principaliter et ante omnia, Domino, se ipsos et omnia sua ad cultum et gloriam Dei ordinantes; deinde dederunt se ipsos nobis per filialem obedientiam et caritativam subjectionem: et hoc, per voluntatem Dei, id est causa Dei, seu propter divinæ voluntatis beneplacitum et honorem: quoniam Deus requirit ut prælatis vicariis suis obediatur sicut et sibi. Ita ut rogaremus Titum, ut quemadmodum cœpit, ita et perficiat in vobis etiam gratiam istam, id est, ad tantam perfectionem, tamque liberalem eleemosynæ distributionem vos conetur inducere, instruendo, hortando, et alios in exemplum vobis proponendo, quemadmodum dudum jam facere incepit in vobis.
paras.en: [[8:5|And not as we hoped|Et non sicut speravimus]], that is, they did not keep to so moderate a measure in giving as we expected, [[8:5|but they gave their own selves|sed semetipsos dederunt]], that is, offered them, [[8:5|first|primum]], that is, chiefly and before all things, [[8:5|to the Lord|Domino]], ordering themselves and all they had to the worship and glory of God; [[8:5|then|deinde]] they gave themselves [[8:5|to us|nobis]] by filial obedience and charitable subjection: and this [[8:5|by the will of God|per voluntatem Dei]], that is, for God's sake, or for the good pleasure and honour of the divine will: since God requires that his vicars the prelates be obeyed as he himself is[[Luke 10:16||]]. [[8:6|Insomuch, that we desired Titus, that, as he had begun, so also he would finish among you this same grace|Ita ut rogaremus Titum, ut quemadmodum cœpit, ita et perficiat in vobis etiam gratiam istam]], that is, that he would try to lead you to so great a perfection and so liberal a distribution of alms, by instructing, exhorting, and setting others before you as an example, as he already began to do among you some time ago.

paras.t: Sed sicut in omnibus gratiarum charismatibus abundatis, videlicet fide qua certi estis de præmio, et sermone, id est efficacia in loquendo, et scientia Scripturarum, et omni sollicitudine in providendo vobis ac aliis, præsertim in spiritualibus bonis, et item in temporalibus, prout ratio exigit; insuper et caritate vestra tendente in nos, quoniam multum diligitis me tanquam magistrum veritatis, et patrem vestræ spiritualis regenerationis: sic cupio ut et in hac gratia misericordiæ et liberalitatis abundetis. Non quasi imperans dico, id est, ad eleemosynam istam non obligo vos præcepto, ne efficiamini transgressores mandati, sed per aliorum, puta Macedonum, sollicitudinem imitatione dignam, etiam vestræ caritatis ingenium bonum, id est vestræ dilectionis indolem seu industriam, comprobans sive experiens, an scilicet sic agatis, sicut confidimus.
paras.en: [[8:7|That as in all things|Sed sicut in omnibus]] gifts of grace [[8:7|you abound|abundatis]], namely [[8:7|in faith|videlicet fide]], by which you are certain of the reward, [[8:7|and word|et sermone]], that is, power in speaking, [[8:7|and knowledge|et scientia]] of the Scriptures, [[8:7|and all carefulness|et omni sollicitudine]] in providing for yourselves and for others, above all in spiritual goods, and also in temporal ones, as reason requires; [[8:7|moreover also in your charity towards us|insuper et caritate vestra tendente in nos]], since you love me greatly as a master of truth and the father of your spiritual regeneration: so I desire [[8:7|so in this grace also|ut et in hac gratia]] of mercy and liberality [[8:7|you may abound|abundetis]]. [[8:8|I speak not as commanding|Non quasi imperans dico]], that is, I do not bind you to this alms by a precept, lest you become transgressors of a command, [[8:8|but by the carefulness of others|sed per aliorum]], namely of the Macedonians, a carefulness worthy of imitation, [[8:8|approving also|comprobans]], or putting to the test, [[8:8|the good disposition of your charity|etiam vestræ caritatis ingenium bonum]], that is, the natural bent or diligence of your love: whether, that is, you act as we trust you will.

paras.t: Porro ad hanc perfectionem invitat eos Apostolus exemplo Christi. Scitis enim per fidem gratiam, id est beneficia vel caritatem, Domini nostri Jesu Christi ad nos. Quoniam propter vos egenus factus est in sua incarnatione et conversatione in hoc mundo. Propter quod ait: Vulpes foveas habent, et volucres cœli nidos; Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput reclinet. Natus quoque, positus est in præsepio, quia non erat ei locus in diversorio. Unde scriptum est: Exsulta, filia Sion, ecce Rex tuus venit tibi justus et salvator; ipse pauper, et ascendens super asinam. Hanc paupertatem vehementissime admiratus est Jeremias, clamans: Quare quasi colonus venturus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum? Quum dives esset, in divina natura habens omnium bonorum atque pulchrorum plenitudinem infinitam simpliciterque perfectam. Ut illius inopia, id est merito paupertatis Christi, vos divites essetis, id est, spiritualium bonorum copiam consequeremini. Nam Christi incarnatio, nostra deificatio est; Christi conversatio, nostra est perfectio; Christi penuria, nostra est opulentia.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle invites them to this perfection by the example of Christ. [[8:9|For you know|Scitis enim]] by faith [[8:9|the grace|gratiam]], that is, the benefits or the charity, [[8:9|of our Lord Jesus Christ|Domini nostri Jesu Christi]] towards us, that [[8:9|he became poor for your sakes|Quoniam propter vos egenus factus est]] in his incarnation and his life in this world. For this reason he says: [[Matt 8:20|The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head|Vulpes foveas habent, et volucres cœli nidos; Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput reclinet]]. Also, at his birth he was laid [[Luke 2:7|in a manger: because there was no room for them in the inn|in præsepio, quia non erat ei locus in diversorio]]. Whence it is written: [[Zach 9:9|Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion|Exsulta, filia Sion]], [[Zach 9:9|BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee, the just and saviour: he is poor, and riding upon an ass|ecce Rex tuus venit tibi justus et salvator; ipse pauper, et ascendens super asinam]]. Jeremias marvelled most vehemently at this poverty, crying: [[Jer 14:8|why wilt thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man turning in to lodge?|Quare quasi colonus venturus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum?]]? [[8:9|being rich|Quum dives esset]], having in the divine nature an infinite and simply perfect fullness of all good and beautiful things. [[8:9|that through his poverty|Ut illius inopia]], that is, by the merit of Christ's poverty, [[8:9|you might be rich|vos divites essetis]], that is, might gain an abundance of spiritual goods. For Christ's incarnation is our deification; Christ's way of life is our perfection; Christ's want is our wealth.

paras.t: Et consilium in hoc do, videlicet ut eleemosynam detis ex hac consideratione: Hoc enim vobis utile est, id est meritorium vitæ æternæ, qui non solum facere, sed et velle per caritatem cœpistis ab anno priore, id est præterito. Nunc vero et facto perficite, id est, opere adimplete; ut quemadmodum promptus ad dandum est animus, id est amorosus impetus, voluntatis, ita sit et perficiendi animus promptus in vobis ex eo quod habetis, id est ex facultatibus seu substantiis vestris, quatenus opere ostendatis et exsequamini in effectu, quod diu inchoastis et proposuistis. Si enim voluntas prompta est dare eleemosynam; secundum id quod habet, accepta est, id est, dando quod sibi in promptu est et superest, seu superfluit, grata et placens est Deo, non secundum id quod non habet, id est, non exigitur ut ultra vires vel sibi necessaria tribuat. Unde in Evangelio ait Salvator: Quod superest, date eleemosynam, et omnia munda sunt vobis.
paras.en: [[8:10|And herein I give my advice|Et consilium in hoc do]], namely that you give alms from this consideration: [[8:10|for this is profitable for you|Hoc enim vobis utile est]], that is, meritorious of eternal life, [[8:10|who have begun not only to do but also to be willing|qui non solum facere, sed et velle]] through charity, [[8:10|a year ago|cœpistis ab anno priore]], that is, last year. [[8:11|Now therefore perform ye it also in deed|Nunc vero et facto perficite]], that is, fulfil it in work; [[8:11|that as your mind is forward|ut quemadmodum promptus ad dandum est animus]] to give, that is, the loving impulse, [[8:11|to be willing|voluntatis]], [[8:11|so it may be also to perform|ita sit et perficiendi animus promptus in vobis]], the mind being forward in you, [[8:11|out of that which you have|ex eo quod habetis]], that is, out of your means or goods, so that you may show in work and carry out in effect what you long ago began and purposed. [[8:12|For if the will be forward|Si enim voluntas prompta est]] to give alms, [[8:12|it is accepted according to that which a man hath|secundum id quod habet, accepta est]], that is, in giving what it has at hand and to spare, or what is superfluous, it is pleasing and acceptable to God, [[8:12|not according to that which he hath not|non secundum id quod non habet]], that is, it is not required that one give beyond one's strength, or what is necessary to oneself.
